модуль ara::per — Persistency

Спецификация: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf (R25-11) · 140 записей API

function: 116 class: 10 enumeration: 6 variable: 5 type alias: 2 struct: 1

Руководство пользователя Сгенерировано ИИ / AI generated

Автоматически создаваемое описание, контент получен из ссылочных документов AUTOSAR R25-11 (спецификация SWS и сопроводительные стандартные документы) — не официальный текст AUTOSAR. Утверждения, помеченные как интерпретация, представляют собой выводы, сделанные на основе источников.

Назначение и граница системы

ara::per делает настроенные постоянные данные доступными для адаптивных приложений. Модель различает Key-Value Storages как наборы типизированных пар ключ-значение и File Storages как наборы именованных файлов; оба могут быть объединены в одном приложении. SWS Persistency §7.1 «The Architecture of Persistency»

Экземпляр хранилища не может быть выбран свободно, но он ссылается на проявленный интерфейс персистентности с помощью ara::core::InstanceSpecifier. Права доступа могут быть только чтение, чтение/запись, только запись или – для приложений – только однократная запись. SWS Persistency §7.1.1 «Configuration of Persistency»

Решение: ключ или файл

Выбирайте KeyValueStorage для адресуемых, типизированных состояний с явной границей синхронизации; выбирайте FileStorage для файлового содержимого и чтения либо записи на основе Accessor. Начальные значения и начальные файлы могут поставляться с Installation или Update. SWS Persistency §7.1.2 «Configuration of Key-Value Storages» SWS Persistency §7.1.3 «Configuration of File Storages»

Интерпретация: Выбор зависит от модели данных: небольшие, логически разделенные состояния получают выгоду от ключей; Непрерывный или потоковый контент больше подходит для файлового интерфейса. Это следует из различных моделей доступа, описанных в спецификации.

Операционная модель и надежность данных

Открытое хранилище ключей-значений изначально работает с временными данными. SyncToStorage постоянно записывает все изменения с момента открытия или последней синхронизации и обновляет настроенную избыточность; Без синхронизации изменения отменяются при закрытии или перезапуске. SWS Persistency §7.3 «Key-Value Storage specific Features»

Для файлов конкретный файл открывается с помощью средства доступа. Доступ на запись может быть специально перенесен в физическую память через SyncToFile; Право собственности на средство доступа является исключительным. SWS Persistency §7.4 «File Storage specific Features»

Защита, восстановление и ресурсы

Избыточность может обеспечить целостность с помощью контрольных сумм или нескольких копий; в случае неисправимых результатов обратный вызов отчета о восстановлении может сообщить приложению. Восстановление может привести к использованию исходных или более старых данных, поэтому его необходимо проверить профессионально. SWS Persistency §7.2.4 «Redundancy Concepts»

Настроенный максимум ограничивает фактическую используемую память. Запросы размера включают метаданные, а также потребности в избыточности и резервном копировании и могут быть неточными для открытого хранилища или параллельных операций. SWS Persistency §7.2.6 «Resource Management Concepts»

Установка, обновление и откат

Целевая конфигурация может содержать предопределенные значения и файлы. На этапе проверки UpdatePersistency может выполнять изменения в соответствии с новыми данными конфигурации; После успешной финализации CleanUpPersistency удаляет данные резервной копии. Если активирована более старая конфигурация, будет выполнено восстановление или новая установка в зависимости от сохраненной версии резервной копии. SWS Persistency §7.2.5 «Installation and Update of Persistent Data»

Для открытия требуется настроенное, инициализированное постоянство. Источники: SWS Persistency §7.1 «The Architecture of Persistency» SWS Persistency §7.3 «Key-Value Storage specific Features».

Граница персистирования распространяется на все ключи, изменённые с момента открытия либо последней синхронизации; сюда относится и обновлённая настроенная избыточность. Источник: SWS Persistency §7.3 «Key-Value Storage specific Features».

Восстановление – это лучшее, что можно сделать; В случае ошибки в отчете можно указать имя затронутого хранилища или элементов. Источник: SWS Persistency §7.2.4 «Redundancy Concepts». Частичная интерпретация: последовательность действий объединяет несколько разрешенных дублирующих процедур.

Update, финализация и Rollback закреплены в версионировании Target-Configuration. Источники: SWS Persistency §7.2.5 «Installation and Update of Persistent Data». Частичная интерпретация: расположение показывает предусмотренный рабочий процесс, а не сигнализацию отдельного вызова API.

Du bist der offizielle KI-Kurations-Assistent für das autodocs Dokumentations- und Spezifikationssystem (AUTOSAR & S-Core).
Deine Aufgabe ist es, präzise, fachlich fundierte Erklärungen, User Guides und Diagramme zu verfassen.

FOLGENDE RICHTLINIEN SIND STRIKT BINDEND:
# Richtlinien für KI-generierte Erklärungen

Diese Datei ist Teil des Kuratierungsprozesses: Sie enthält die inhaltlichen
Leitplanken für alle KI-generierten Texte und Diagramme. Die maschinenlesbaren
Parameter dazu stehen in `ai/policy.json`; beide werden von
`ai_workflow.py auftrag` wörtlich in jeden Regenerierungsauftrag eingebettet.
Änderungen an Policy oder Richtlinien ⇒ `version` in `policy.json` erhöhen;
`ai_workflow.py status` zeigt dann, welche Fragmente noch mit einer älteren
Version erzeugt wurden.

## Geltungsbereich und Sprache

- Kanonische Sprache ist Deutsch (`site.json → sprachen.kanonisch`). KI-Inhalte
  werden ausschließlich deutsch erzeugt; die Übersetzung ist ein nachgelagerter
  Schritt (i18n_*.py) und niemals Teil der Generierung.
- API-Bezeichner, Typnamen, Enum-Werte, Code und `[SWS_…]`-Kennungen bleiben
  in jeder Sprache unverändert.

## Strukturelle Invarianten

- Jedes Fragment ist genau ein `<div class="ai …">` (Varianten: `ai` für
  Abschnitte, `ai usage` für Verwendungshinweise an Records, `ai module-guide`
  für Modul-Leitfäden) mit Badge und abschließender `<p class="ai-note">`
  (KI-Hinweis). Bestehende Fragmente sind die Referenz.
- Fragmente liegen unter `content/ai/<seiten-verzeichnis>/` und heißen
  `rec_<ELEMENT-ID>_<NN>.html` (an ein Spezifikationselement gebunden) oder
  `main_<NN>.html` (seitenbezogen).

## Belegpflicht und Quellen

- Jede fachliche Aussage ist mit `[SWS_…]`/`[RS_…]`-Zitat zu belegen
  (`policy.zitierpflicht`); Zitate verlinken auf das Quelldokument (PDF mit
  `#nameddest`), Richtwert `policy.relevanz.min_zitate_je_absatz`.
- Es dürfen nur Dokumente aus dem Quellenregister `ai/quellen.json` verwendet
  werden. Neue Quellen werden zuerst dort registriert (id, titel, typ, url).
- Aus Quellen extrahierte Einzelaussagen, auf die sich ein Text stützt, werden
  in der Trace unter `wissen[]` festgehalten: `{"aussage": …, "quelle": <id>,
  "fundstelle": …}`.

## Annahmen (Wissenslücken)

- Wo die Spezifikation schweigt, darf die KI Lücken mit Annahmen schließen —
  höchstens `policy.annahmen.budget_je_text` pro Text bzw.
  `budget_je_diagramm` pro Diagramm.
- Jede Annahme wird (a) im Text als Interpretation erkennbar formuliert und
  (b) in der Trace unter `annahmen[]` protokolliert:
  `{"annahme": …, "begruendung": …}`.
- Reicht das Budget nicht, wird der Aspekt weggelassen — niemals unmarkiert
  spekuliert.

## Diagramm-Entscheidung

Ein Diagramm wird nur eingefügt, wenn es gegenüber dem Text Mehrwert bietet
(`policy.diagramme`):

- Sequenzdiagramm (`.seq.json`): Abläufe mit ≥ `sequenz_ab_schritten`
  Schritten oder nicht offensichtlicher Reihenfolge/Asynchronität.
- Kontext-/Strukturdiagramm (`.dot`): ≥ `kontext_ab_beteiligten` beteiligte
  Komponenten oder nicht-triviale Vererbungs-/Abhängigkeitscluster.
- Zustandsdiagramm (`.dot`): Lebenszyklen und Zustandsmaschinen.
- Keine Trivialdiagramme (einzelne Aufrufe, Getter/Setter, Zweierbeziehungen).

Die Entscheidung („warum dieses Diagramm, warum diese Form“), etwaige
Annahmen und das Denk-Transkript zur Quellenerstellung gehören in die Trace
unter `diagramme["<quellpfad>"]` — nicht ins HTML. Diagrammquellen liegen als
`<fragment-stem>.<diag-id>.dot|.seq.json` neben dem Fragment (inline) bzw.
unter `diagrams/` (seitenweite Diagramme); gerendert wird mit
`render_diagrams.py`. Beschriftungen deutsch, Bezeichner unverändert.

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\">template &lt;class T&gt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; SetValue (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> key, const T &amp;value) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Stores a key-value pair in this Key-Value Storage. If a value already exists and has the same data type as the new value, it is overwritten. If the new value has a different data type than the stored value, kDataTypeMismatch is returned. SetValue may be delayed by an ongoing call from another thread to RemoveAllKeys, SyncTo Storage, or DiscardPendingChanges, or to SetValue, GetValue, GetCurrentValueSize, Remove Key, RecoverKey, or ResetKey for the same key-value pair. This method uses transaction semantics, the changes only take effect when SyncToStorage is called.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Removes a key and the associated value from this Key-Value Storage.       {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_per_SharedHandle_a773d0.html\">SharedHandle</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_per_KeyValueStorage_e55123.html\">KeyValueStorage</a> &gt; &gt; OpenKeyValue Storage (const <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_core_InstanceSpecifier_4f5967.html\">ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</a> &amp;kvs) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a Key-Value Storage. OpenKeyValueStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently being modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset Persistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage. Because multiple threads can access the same Key-Value Storage concurrently, the Key-Value Storage might not be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of scope. It will only be closed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same Key-Value Storage went out of scope.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_per_UniqueHandle_94e9f0.html\">UniqueHandle</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_per_ReadWriteAccessor_30aeb5.html\">ReadWriteAccessor</a> &gt; &gt; OpenFileRead Write (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> fileName, <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_per_ara_per_d9a3e9.html#SWS_PER_00147\">OpenMode</a> mode) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a file of this File Storage for reading and writing with a defined mode. If not otherwise specified by the provided mode, the file is opened with the seek position set to the beginning (corresponding to kAtTheBeginning). If the file does not exist, it is created. The file will be closed when the returned UniqueHandle goes out of scope.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a File Storage. OpenFileStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently being modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency, RecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles. Because multiple threads can access the same File Storage concurrently, the File Storage might not be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of scope. It will only be closed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same File Storage went out of scope.</p></div>",

        "tail": "\n"

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html#SWS_CORE_03001\">ara::core::String</a> &gt; ReadLine (char delimiter=’\\n’) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Reads a complete line of characters into a String, advancing the current position accordingly. The end of the line is demarcated by the delimiter, or by \"\\\\n\" (ASCII 0x0a) if that parameter is omitted. The delimiter itself is not included in the returned String. Only Unicode code points with one character (code unit) can be used as delimiters. The returned string may start with an incomplete Unicode code point in case the current read position is in the middle of a code point. If the end of the file is reached, the remaining characters are returned and the current position is set to the end of the file. In case of an error, the current position is not changed.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {

        "src": "content/ai/classes/cl_ara_per_ReadAccessor_4ffb0b/rec_SWS_PER_00119_08.html",

title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00159</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html#SWS_CORE_03001\">ara::core::String</a> &gt; ReadText (<a class=\"cppref\" href=\"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/integer\" title=\"cppreference.com (C++17)\">std::uint64_t</a> n) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Reads a number of characters into a String, starting from the current position. The returned string may start and/or end with incomplete Unicode code points in case the current read position and/or the last read character (code unit) is in the middle of a code point. The current position is advanced accordingly. If the end of the file is reached, the number of returned characters can be less than the requested number, and the current position is set to the end of the file. In case of an error, the current position is not changed.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

        "t": "ai",
        "src": "content/ai/classes/cl_ara_per_ReadAccessor_4ffb0b/rec_SWS_PER_00165_09.html",

<a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00127\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00135</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00136\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00136</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00139\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00139</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00159\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00159</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; WriteText (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> s) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Writes the content of a StringView to the file. The time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo File can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content. In case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might not have changed. The expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows: • kPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely destroyed. • kEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but could not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file. • kOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the operation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at the end of the file.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "ai",
        "src": "content/ai/classes/cl_ara_per_WriteAccessor_a926f9/rec_SWS_PER_00166_05.html",
        "tail": "\n"
      }
    ],

href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00159\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00159</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; ResetKeyValueStorage (const <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_core_InstanceSpecifier_4f5967.html\">ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</a> &amp;kvs) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a Key-Value Storage to the initial state. ResetKeyValueStorage allows to reset a Key-Value Storage to the initial state, containing only key-value pairs which were deployed from the Target Configuration, with their initial values. Afterwards, the Key-Value Storage will appear as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration. It will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently open, or when it is modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset Persistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; ResetAllFiles (const <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html\">ara::core::Instance</a> Specifier &amp;fs) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a File Storage, including all files. ResetAllFiles resets a File Storage to the initial state, containing only the files which were deployed from the Target Configuration, with their initial content. Afterwards, the File Storage will appear as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration. It will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently open, or when it is modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency, RecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

(AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00139</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00159\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00159</a></span></h3>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; ResetFile (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> fileName) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a file of this File Storage to its initial content. ResetFile allows to reset a single file to its initial content. If the file is currently not available in the File Storage, it is re-created. Afterwards, the file will appear in both cases as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration. It will fail with kResourceBusy when the file is currently open, and with kInitValueNotAvailable when neither Application Design nor Target Configuration define an initial content for the file.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "ai",
        "src": "content/ai/classes/cl_ara_per_FileStorage_29266b/rec_SWS_PER_00338_17.html",
        "tail": "\n"
      }
    ],
    "SWS_PER_00350": [
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<h3 class=\"recname\"><span class=\"kind\">function</span> ThrowAsException <span class=\"sws\"><a href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=SWS_PER_00350\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf)\">[SWS_PER_00350]</a></span> <span class=\"ups\">Upstream: <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00120\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00120</a>, <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf#nameddest=RS_AP_00121\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_RS_General.pdf)\">RS_AP_00121</a></span></h3>",

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\">void ThrowAsException (const <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_ErrorCode_538b08.html\">ara::core::ErrorCode</a> &amp;errorCode) const noexcept(false) override;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Throws the exception associated with the error code. As per <a class=\"swsref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf#nameddest=SWS_CORE_10304\" title=\"Spezifikations-PDF (AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core.pdf)\">[SWS_CORE_10304]</a>, this function does not participate in overload resolution when C++ exceptions are disabled in the compiler toolchain.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n\n"
      },

        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Returns the space in bytes currently occupied by a Key-Value Storage. The returned size includes all metadata and the space used for redundancy and backups. The returned size is only guaranteed to be accurate if the Key-Value Storage is not opened and no other operation on the Key-Value Storage takes place at the same time.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Vector_53b788.html\">ara::core::Vector</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html#SWS_CORE_04200\">ara::core::Byte</a> &gt; &gt; ReadBinary (<a class=\"cppref\" href=\"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/integer\" title=\"cppreference.com (C++17)\">std::uint64_t</a> n) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Reads a number of bytes into a Vector of Byte, starting from the current position. The current position is advanced accordingly. If the end of the file is reached, the number of returned bytes can be less than the requested number, and the current position is set to the end of the file. In case of an error, the current position is not changed.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; WriteBinary (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Span_f16d72.html\">ara::core::Span</a>&lt; const <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html#SWS_CORE_04200\">ara::core::Byte</a> &gt; b) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Writes the content of a Span of Byte to the file. The time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo File can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content. In case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might not have changed. The expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows: • kPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely destroyed. • kEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but could not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file. • kOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the operation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at the end of the file.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      }

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; ResetKey (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> key) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Resets a key of this Key-Value Storage to its initial value. ResetKey allows to reset a single key to its initial value. If the key is currently not available in the Key-Value Storage, it is re-created. Afterwards, the key-value pair will appear in both cases as if it was newly installed from the current Target Configuration. ResetKey will fail with kInitValueNotAvailable when neither Application Design nor Target Configuration define an initial value for the key. ResetKey may be delayed by an ongoing call from another thread to RemoveAllKeys, SyncTo Storage, or DiscardPendingChanges, or to SetValue, GetValue, GetCurrentValueSize, Remove Key, RecoverKey, or ResetKey for the same key-value pair.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; RecoverKey (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> key) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Recovers a single key-value pair of this Key Value Storage. This method allows to recover a single key-value pair when the redundancy checks fail. This method does a best-effort recovery of the key-value pair. After recovery, the key-value pair might contain outdated or initial content, or might be lost. RecoverKey may be delayed by an ongoing call from another thread to RemoveAllKeys, SyncTo Storage, or DiscardPendingChanges, or to SetValue, GetValue, GetCurrentValueSize, Remove Key, RecoverKey, or ResetKey for the same key-value pair.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_per_UniqueHandle_94e9f0.html\">UniqueHandle</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_per_ReadWriteAccessor_30aeb5.html\">ReadWriteAccessor</a> &gt; &gt; OpenFileRead Write (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> fileName, <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_per_ara_per_d9a3e9.html#SWS_PER_00147\">OpenMode</a> mode, <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Span_f16d72.html\">ara::core::Span</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../namespaces/ns_core_ara_core_e30e31.html#SWS_CORE_04200\">ara::core::Byte</a> &gt; buffer) noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a file of this File Storage for reading and writing with a user provided buffer. If not otherwise specified by the provided mode, the file is opened with the seek position set to the beginning (corresponding to kAtTheBeginning). The provided buffer will be used by the ReadWriteAccessor to implement block-wise reading and writing to speed up multiple small accesses to the file. If the file does not exist, it is created. The file will be closed when the returned UniqueHandle goes out of scope.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a file of this File Storage for reading with a user provided buffer. If not otherwise specified by the provided mode, the file is opened with the seek position set to the beginning (corresponding to kAtTheBeginning). The provided buffer will be used by the ReadAccessor to implement block-wise reading to speed up multiple small accesses to the file. The file will be closed when the returned UniqueHandle goes out of scope.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Opens a file of this File Storage for writing with a user provided buffer. If not otherwise specified by the provided mode, the file is truncated (corresponding to k Truncate). The provided buffer will be used by the ReadWriteAccessor to implement block-wise writing to speed up multiple small accesses to the file. If the file does not exist, it is created. The file will be closed when the returned UniqueHandle goes out of scope.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_per_FileInfo_15b6f6.html\">FileInfo</a> &gt; GetFileInfo (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> file Name) const noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Returns additional information on a file of this File Storage. The returned FileInfo struct contains information about the times when the file was created, last modified, and last accessed, and about how and by whom the file was created and last modified. The modificationTime, accessTime, and fileModificationState returned in the FileInfo are only accurate if the file is currently not open.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"

        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; <a class=\"cppref\" href=\"https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/integer\" title=\"cppreference.com (C++17)\">std::uint64_t</a> &gt; GetCurrentValueSize (<a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"cl_ara_core_StringView_cfeb8f.html\">ara::core::StringView</a> key) const noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Returns the size (in bytes) of the value assigned to a key of this Key-Value Storage. GetCurrentValueSize may be delayed by an ongoing call from another thread to RemoveAllKeys or DiscardPendingChanges, or to SetValue, RemoveKey, RecoverKey, or ResetKey for the same key-value pair. This method uses transaction semantics, it sees the current state of transaction, not the actual physical storage.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Checks for updates of the Persistency Target Configuration. This method can be used to detect configuration updates that are installed by UCM while the Adaptive Application that uses Persistency is running. To re-read the updated Target Configuration, the Adaptive Application needs to call <a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"ns_per_ara_per_d9a3e9.html\">ara::per</a>:: ReloadPersistencyManifest.</p></div>",

      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<pre class=\"syntax\"><a class=\"vis-app\" href=\"../classes/cl_ara_core_Result_d51722.html\">ara::core::Result</a>&lt; void &gt; ReloadPersistencyManifest () noexcept;</pre>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },
      {
        "t": "html",
        "html": "<div class=\"desc\"><p>Re-reads the Target Configuration. This method can be used to prepare for updates of the Key-Value Storages and File Storages of Persistency after a new Target Configuration was installed by UCM while the Adaptive Application that uses Persistency is running. Storages are only updated after closing them, either when they are opened again or by an explicit call to ara:: per::UpdatePersistency.</p></div>",
        "tail": "\n"
      },

195\nD.10.6 Deleted Constraints in R23-11 . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . 195\nE Not Applicable Requirements 196\n9 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P10_14",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 10,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n1 Introduction and Functional Overview\nThis document is the software specification of the\nPersistency functional\ncluster\nwithin the\nAdaptive Platform\n. The\nPersistency functional clus-\nter\nwill be referenced as\nPersistency\nin the remainder of this document.\nPersistency\noffers mechanisms to\nAdaptive Applications\nand other\nfunc-\ntional clusters\nto store information in the non-volatile memory of a machine. The\ndata is available over boot and ignition cycles.\nThe\nPersistency\nwill typically be implemented as a library that runs within a\nPro-\ncess\nof an\nAdaptive Application\n, with the rights of that\nProcess\n.\n10 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_15",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n2 Acronyms and Abbreviations\nThe glossary below includes acronyms and abbreviations relevant to the\nPersis-\ntency\nthat are not included in the [1, AUTOSAR glossary]."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_16",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "This version identifies the structural layout of\nPersistency\n.\nThe\ncontract version\nis expected to change when\nStor-\nages\nare added, removed, or renamed, when their access mode\nchanges, or when the available data types of a\nKey-Value\nStorage\nor the data types of\nstorage elements\nchange."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_17",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "This version identifies the pre-installed content of\nPersistency\n.\nThe\ndeployment version\nis expected to change when pre-\ninstalled\nelements\nof otherwise unchanged\nstorages\nare\nadded, removed, or renamed."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_18",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\ndistinguishes data integrity, which is ensured by\nthe configured\nredundancy\n, from structural integrity, i.e. the\nreadability of the structure of a\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile\nStorage\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P11_19",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 11,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "11 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_20",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_21",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\nsupports different mechanisms to access data in\npersistent memory. Concurrent access to the data by several\nProcess\nes is not supported as the data is owned exclusively by\none\nProcess\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_22",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The actual physical memory on which\npersistent data\nis\nstored. This could be a flash device that is accessed directly\nby\nPersistency\n, or a file system of the OS that uses an SSD."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_23",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Redundancy is used by\nPersistency\nto ensure the\nin-\ntegrity\nof stored data. It can be configured to use replication\nof stored data, CRCs, or Hashes. Typically, only replication will\nallow to repair corrupted data."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_24",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\nuses update strategies configured on\nelement\nand\nstorage\nlevel. The actual\nupdate strategy\nof an\nel-\nement\nis derived from\nmanifest\nparameters for the\nelement\nand the containing\nstorage\ndefined during design and deploy-\nment phase."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P12_25",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 12,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "12 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P13_26",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 13,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n3 Related Documentation\n3.1 Input Documents & Related Standards and Norms\n[1] Glossary\nAUTOSAR_FO_TR_Glossary\n[2] Specification of Adaptive Platform Core\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Core\n[3] Specification of Manifest\nAUTOSAR_AP_TPS_ManifestSpecification\n[4] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Software Architecture\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_SWArchitecture\n[5] Requirements on Persistency\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_Persistency\n[6] General Requirements specific to Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_RS_General\n[7] Specification of Update and Configuration Management\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_UpdateAndConfigurationManagement\n[8] Explanation of Adaptive Platform Design\nAUTOSAR_AP_EXP_PlatformDesign\n[9] Specification of Cryptography\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Cryptography\n[10] Specification of Platform Types for Adaptive Platform\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_PlatformTypes\n[11] Specification of Language Binding for modeled AP data types\nAUTOSAR_AP_SWS_LanguageBindingForModeledAPdatatypes\n3.2 Further Applicable Specifications\nAUTOSAR provides a core specification [2] which is also applicable for the\nPersis-\ntency\n. The chapter General requirements for all FunctionalClusters of this specifica-\ntion shall be considered as an additional and required specification for implementation\nof the\nPersistency\n.\n13 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P14_27",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 14,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4 Constraints and Assumptions\n4.1 Known Limitations\n\u000f\nAlthough a\nKey-Value Storage\nand\nFile Storage\ncan be configured as\nwrite-only, the current API always allows read access. Read access is even pos-\nsible when a\nfile\nhas been opened with\nara::per::FileStorage::Open-\nFileWriteOnly\n.\n4.2 Constraints on Configuration\nThere are several constraints on the\nPersistency\nconfiguration that need to be ob-\nserved by the tooling which creates/processes this part of the\nExecution Manifest\n.\nThese constraints are defined in [3].\n4.3 Assumptions about the Implementation of Persistency\nPersistency\ncan be implemented with different internal architectures, and at the\nsame time,\napplications\nand other\nfunctional clusters\nexpect a well defined\nbehavior that is independent of the actual implementation of\nPersistency\n. There-\nfore, the specification in this document needs to be sufficiently generic to cover the\nunderlying differences. As usual in AUTOSAR Adaptive, the actual implementation is\nnot defined by the specification and is therefore entirely up to the vendor of\nPersis-\ntency\n.\nThe following subsections list some of the possible implementations of\nPersistency\n.\n4.3.1 Library Only\nIn this scenario,\nPersistency\nconsists solely of a library. The manifest is partly used\nto configure the compilation of the library (design time parts) and partly transferred to\na configuration file that is read by\nPersistency\nat run-time (deployment parts).\nThere is still some freedom regarding the storage of\nmetadata\nand actual data, and\nregarding the points in time when\nelements\nof a\nstorage\nare checked regarding re-\ndundancy or authenticity or when they are decrypted. E.g. the whole\nFile Storage\ncould be checked when it is opened or the single\nfiles\ncould be checked when they\nare opened.\n14 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P15_28",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 15,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4.3.2 Using a Central Daemon\nIn this scenario, the\nPersistency\nlibrary connects in the background to a daemon\nvia some IPC mechanism. The manifest influences again the compilation of the library\npart and is also transferred to configuration files for the library part and possibly also\nthe daemon.\nAn implementer has the same freedom regarding data storage, encryption, and checks\nfor redundancy and authenticity as in the last scenario. But an additional challenge is\nthat the communication channel between library and daemon can be lost at any time,\nresulting in additional potential errors.\n4.3.3 Based on a File System\nBoth a library and a daemon can access\nstorage\nusing the file system services of\nthe operating system. In this case, because AUTOSAR Adaptive is based on POSIX,\nthe file systems will be mounted with specific options that are out of control of the\nPersistency\nimplementation, but influence the point in time when written data ac-\ntually appears on the disc. Due to this, it is not possible to guarantee synchronous\nbehavior for calls like\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nor\nara::\nper::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\n.\n4.3.4 Direct Access to Storage Hardware\nIndependently of whether a daemon is used or not,\nPersistency\ncan be implemented\nto access hardware devices like flash memory directly. These devices have the intrinsic\nproblem that the signal that can be read from each memory cell is reduced over time,\nmainly influenced by the number of write accesses. In the end, the cell will produce\narbitrary values on each read access.\nUnfortunately, the distribution of write accesses in typical systems is very uneven.\nSome parameters might be updated a few times a second, while some code may stay\nuntouched for the whole life time of the ECU. To avoid early read errors, wear leveling\nshould be deployed, such that frequent updates of single data elements are distributed\nover the whole memory area.\nOn the other hand, most operating systems include a file system or at least a flash\ndriver that takes care of wear leveling, such that a typical implementation of the\nPer-\nsistency\nwill not have to care about the wear leveling. This use case is therefore not\ndescribed in any detail in this specification.\n15 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_29",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n5 Dependencies to Other Functional Clusters\nThis chapter provides an overview of the dependencies to other\nFunctional Clus-\nters\nin the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n. Section 5.1 Provided Interfaces lists\nthe direct interfaces provided by\nPersistency\nto other\nFunctional Clusters\n.\nSection 5.2 Required Interfaces lists the interfaces required by\nPersistency\n.\nA detailed technical architecture documentation of the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Plat-\nform\nis provided in [4, EXP SW Architecture].\n5.1 Provided Interfaces"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P16_30",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 16,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.1: Interfaces Provided by Persistency to Other Functional Clusters\nFigure 5.1 Interfaces Provided by Persistency to Other Functional Clusters shows the\nKey-Value Storage\ninterfaces provided by\nPersistency\nto other\nFunctional\nClusters\nwithin the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n.\n16 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P17_31",
      "source_element": null,

      "source_page": 17,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P17_32",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 17,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.2: Interfaces Provided by Persistency to Other Functional Clusters\nFigure 5.2 Interfaces Provided by Persistency to Other Functional Clusters shows the\nFile Storage\ninterfaces provided by\nPersistency\nto other\nFunctional Clus-\nters\nwithin the AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P17_33",

    },
    {

      "verbatim_text": "Figure 5.3: Interfaces required by Persistency from other Functional Clusters\n18 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P19_37",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nFigure 5.3 Interfaces required by Persistency from other Functional Clusters shows\nthe interfaces required by\nPersistency\nfrom other\nFunctional Clusters\nwithin\nthe AUTOSAR\nAdaptive Platform\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P19_38",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\nshall use this interface to log standardized\nmessages."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P19_39",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Persistency\nshould use this interface to determine\ntimestamps included in the meta-information of files, e.g.,\nmodification timestamp."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P19_40",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 19,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Table 5.2: Interfaces required from other Functional Clusters\n19 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P20_41",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 20,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n6 Requirements Tracing\nThe following table references the requirements specified in the AUTOSAR RS Per-\nsistency [5] and the AUTOSAR RS General [6], and links to the fulfillments of these.\nPlease note that if column Satisfied by is empty for a specific requirement, this means\nthat this requirement is not fulfilled by this document."
    },
    {

      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 20,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "[SWS_PER_00042] [SWS_PER_00043]\n[SWS_PER_00044] [SWS_PER_00046]\n[SWS_PER_00047] [SWS_PER_00048]\n[SWS_PER_00049] [SWS_PER_00052]\n[SWS_PER_00107] [SWS_PER_00110]\n[SWS_PER_00111] [SWS_PER_00112]\n[SWS_PER_00113] [SWS_PER_00114]\n[SWS_PER_00115] [SWS_PER_00116]\n[SWS_PER_00119] [SWS_PER_00122]\n[SWS_PER_00125] [SWS_PER_00144]\n[SWS_PER_00162] [SWS_PER_00163]\n[SWS_PER_00164] [SWS_PER_00165]\n[SWS_PER_00166] [SWS_PER_00167]\n[SWS_PER_00168] [SWS_PER_00313]\n[SWS_PER_00314] [SWS_PER_00315]\n[SWS_PER_00323] [SWS_PER_00325]\n[SWS_PER_00327] [SWS_PER_00329]\n[SWS_PER_00332] [SWS_PER_00333]\n[SWS_PER_00334] [SWS_PER_00335]\n[SWS_PER_00336] [SWS_PER_00337]\n[SWS_PER_00338] [SWS_PER_00351]\n[SWS_PER_00352] [SWS_PER_00357]\n[SWS_PER_00358] [SWS_PER_00360]\n[SWS_PER_00361] [SWS_PER_00363]\n[SWS_PER_00364] [SWS_PER_00365]\n[SWS_PER_00368] [SWS_PER_00370]\n[SWS_PER_00372] [SWS_PER_00375]\n[SWS_PER_00376] [SWS_PER_00377]\n[SWS_PER_00398] [SWS_PER_00399]\n[SWS_PER_00400] [SWS_PER_00401]\n[SWS_PER_00402] [SWS_PER_00403]\n[SWS_PER_00405] [SWS_PER_00406]\n[SWS_PER_00407] [SWS_PER_00414]\n[SWS_PER_00416] [SWS_PER_00418]\n[SWS_PER_00419] [SWS_PER_00420]\n[SWS_PER_00421] [SWS_PER_00422]\n[SWS_PER_00423] [SWS_PER_00424]\n[SWS_PER_00426] [SWS_PER_00427]\n[SWS_PER_00428] [SWS_PER_00429]\n[SWS_PER_00430] [SWS_PER_00431]\n[SWS_PER_00434] [SWS_PER_00438]\n[SWS_PER_00554] [SWS_PER_00567]"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P31_107",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00446",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 31,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Table 6.1: RequirementsTracing\n31 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P32_108",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7 Functional Specification\n7.1 The Architecture of Persistency\nThe\nPersistency\noffers two different mechanisms to access persistent memory:\nKey-Value Storages\noffer access to a set of\nkeys\nwith associated\nvalues\n(similar\nto a database), while\nFile Storages\noffer access to a set of\nfiles\n(similar to a\ndirectory of a file system).\nThe typical usage of the\nPersistency\nwithin an\nAdaptive Application\nis de-\npicted in Figure 7.1. As shown there, an\nAdaptive Application\ncan use a combi-\nnation of multiple\nKey-Value Storages\nand multiple\nFile Storages\n. Of course,\nthe same applies to other\nfunctional clusters\nusing\nPersistency\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P32_109",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 32,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Figure 7.1: Typical usage of\nPersistency\nwithin an\nAdaptive Application\nPersistency\ncan also be used directly by other\nFunctional Clusters\nwithout\ninvolvement of the\napplication\n. The library part of these\nFunctional Clusters\nwill use dedicated deployment information of\nPersistency\n, while Daemons of\nFunc-\ntional Clusters\ncan be modeled similarly to\nAdaptive Applications\n.\n7.1.1 Persistency in the Manifest\nThe\nPersistency\nusage of an\nAdaptive Application\nis modeled in the\nExe-\ncution Manifest\n(furtheron simply referred to as the \nmanifest\n) as part of the\n32 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P33_110",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nAdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType\ns of an\nExecutable\n. The model has\ntwo principal parts: The application design information, aggregated by the\nPersis-\ntencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nand the\nPersistencyFileStorageInter-\nface\n, and the deployment information, aggregated by the\nPersistencyKeyVal-\nueStorage\nand the\nPersistencyFileStorage\n. The latter is also used when the\nPersistency\nis accessed directly by another\nFunctional Cluster\n.\nThe API specification holds the classes\nara::per::KeyValueStorage\nand\nara::\nper::FileStorage\nfor access to a\nKey-Value Storage\nor a\nFile Storage\n, re-\nspectively. The global functions of these classes receive either the identifier (the fully\nqualified\nshortName\npath) of a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyInter-\nface\n, or the\nshortName\npath of a\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersis-\ntencyDeploymentMapping\n. Both are then used as an\nara::core::Instance-\nSpecifier\ninput parameter (see subsection 8.2.1 and subsection 8.3.1). Depend-\ning on the nature of the\nPortPrototype\nor on the value of\nFunctionalCluster-\nInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\n, the\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nwill be accessible as:\nRead Only\nif the\nPortPrototype\nis instantiated as\nRPortPrototype\nor\nFunc-\ntionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\nis\nread\n, or\nRead/Write\nif the\nPortPrototype\nis instantiated as\nPRPortPrototype\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\nis\nreadWrite\n, or\nWrite Only\nif the\nPortPrototype\nis instantiated as\nPPortPrototype\nor\nFunc-\ntionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\npersistencyAccess\nis\nwrite\n.\nIn case of application access to Persistency, the\nmanifest\ncontains separate de-\nployment data for each\nProcess\nthat references the\nExecutable\n. The\nProcess\nis bound to the deployment data by specialization of the class\nPersistencyPort-\nPrototypeToDeploymentMapping\n, which refers to a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyInterface\n, a\nPersistencyDeployment\n, and the\nProcess\n."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P33_111",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 33,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Usage of base classes in the manifest\nFor simplification reasons, the information that applies to both the\nKey-Value Stor-\nages\nand the\nFile Storages\nis collected in base classes in the\nmanifest\n, namely\nin\nPersistencyInterface\nfor\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nand\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface\n, and in\nPersistencyDeployment\nfor\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nand\nPersistencyFileStorage\n.\nLikewise, the common information about\nkey-value pairs\nand\nfiles\nis collected\nin\nPersistencyInterfaceElement\nfor\nPersistencyDataElement\nand\nPer-\nsistencyFileElement\n, and in\nPersistencyDeploymentElement\nfor\nPersis-\ntencyKeyValuePair\nand\nPersistencyFile\n.\n33 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P34_112",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P34_113",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 34,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "And the link between application design and deployment information, represented by\nPersistencyPortPrototypeToDeploymentMapping\n, is specialized as\nPersis-\ntencyPortPrototypeToKeyValueStorageMapping\nand\nPersistencyPort-\nPrototypeToFileStorageMapping\n.\n7.1.2 Key-Value Storages in the Manifest\nEvery\nKey-Value Storage\nis either represented by a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by\na\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nin the application design for the re-\nspective\nAdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType\n, or by a\nFunctionalClus-\nterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n, and in both cases by a\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\ncontaining deployment information. Every\nKey-\n-Value Storage\ncan hold multiple\nkey-value pairs\n.\nKey-value pairs\ncan\nbe added and removed at run-time by the\nAdaptive Application\nor\nFunctional\nCluster\nusing the\nPersistency\nAPI (see subsubsection 8.2.5.8 and subsubsection\n8.2.5.9).\nA\nKey-Value Storage\nwith predefined\nkey-value pairs\ncan be deployed with\ndefault data during installation or update of an\nAdaptive Application\nor\nFunc-\ntional Cluster\n. This operation is (indirectly) triggered by the\nUpdate and Con-\nfiguration Management\n[7] during installation or update using the deployment in-\nformation and data provided by the\nsoftware package\nof the\nAdaptive Appli-\ncation\nor\nFunctional Cluster\n. See subsection 7.2.6.\nThe link between application design and deployment information of a\nKey-\n-Value Storage\nis represented by\nPersistencyPortPrototypeToKeyVal-\nueStorageMapping\n, which refers to a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersis-\ntencyKeyValueStorageInterface\n, the corresponding\nPersistencyKeyVal-\nueStorage\n, and a\nProcess\n.\n7.1.3 File Storages in the Manifest\nEvery\nFile Storage\nis represented by a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPer-\nsistencyFileStorageInterface\nin the application design for the respective\nAdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType\n, or by a\nFunctionalClusterInter-\nactsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n, and in both cases by a\nPersis-\ntencyFileStorage\ncontaining deployment information. Every\nFile Storage\ncan\nhold multiple\nfiles\nas described in [3]. Similar to the\nkey-value pairs\nmentioned\nabove,\nfiles\ncan be created and deleted at run-time by the\nAdaptive Applica-\ntion\nor\nFunctional Cluster\nusing the\nPersistency\nAPI (see subsubsection\n8.3.11.11, subsubsection 8.3.11.13, and subsubsection 8.3.11.5).\nA\nFile Storage\nwith predefined\nfiles\nwith initial content can be deployed dur-\ning installation or update. This operation is also (indirectly) triggered by the\nUp-\ndate and Configuration Management\n[7]. All needed deployment information\n34 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P35_114",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 35,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nand\nfiles\ncome with the\nsoftware package\nof the\nAdaptive Application\nor\nFunctional Cluster\n. See subsection 7.2.6.\nThe link between application design and deployment information of a\nFile Storage\nis represented by\nPersistencyPortPrototypeToFileStorageMapping\n, which\nrefers to a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface\n, the\ncorresponding\nPersistencyFileStorage\n, and a\nProcess\n.\n35 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P36_115",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00002",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 36,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2 General Features of Persistency\n[SWS_PER_00002]\nd\nAll specified classes within the\nPersistency\nshall reside within\nthe C++ namespace\nara::per\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00115)\n7.2.1 Functional Cluster Lifecycle\n7.2.1.1 Initialization and Shutdown of Persistency\nUsing\nara::core::Initialize\nand\nara::core::Deinitialize\n, the applica-\ntion initializes and de-initializes all\nfunctional clusters\nwith direct ARA interfaces\n(i.e. the\nAdaptive Platform Foundation\n).\n[SWS_PER_00408]\nd\nWhen\nara::core::Initialize\nis called, the\nPersistency\nshall read in the\nmanifest\ninformation and prepare the access structures to all\nKey-\n-Value Storages\nand\nFile Storages\nthat are defined in the\nmanifest\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00018)\n[SWS_PER_00409]\nd\nWhen\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis called, the\nPersis-\ntency\nshall implicitly ensure that all open\nfiles\nof all\nFile Storages\nare per-\nsisted as though\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nwas called and\nclosed as though the\nara::per::UniqueHandle\ns were destructed, and that not\npersisted\nvalues\nin all\nKey-Value Storages\nare dropped as though\nara::per::\nKeyValueStorage::DiscardPendingChanges\nwas called. Afterwards,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall free remaining resources that are not exposed by objects held by the ap-\nplication, including but not limited to the configuration of\nPersistency\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00018)\nThe\napplication\nis expected not to call any API of\nPersistency\n(directly or in-\ndirectly through other\nfunctional clusters\n) before calling\nara::core::Ini-\ntialize\nor after calling\nara::core::Deinitialize\n, but\nPersistency\nneeds to\nprotect itself against such eventualities.\n[SWS_PER_00410]\n{DRAFT}\nd\nAll functions of\nPersistency\nand all methods of its\nclasses shall call\nara::core::Abort\nwhen they are called after static initializa-\ntion but before\nara::core::Initialize\nwas called or after\nara::core::Deini-\ntialize\nwas called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00018)\n36 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P37_116",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00472",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 37,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.2 Error Handling\nError handling in\nPersistency\nis aligned with the guidelines described in [2]. To this\nend, the\nPersistency\nhas to implement a set of standard classes and APIs, which\nare described in this section.\n[SWS_PER_00472]\nd\nPersistency\nshall use the error codes defined in\nara::per::\nPerErrc\nto report problems to the calling\napplication\nvia\nara::core::Result\n.\nVendors of\nPersistency\nmay add their own errors to\nara::per::PerErrc\n, using\ncodes above\n255\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nara::per::PerErrc\nbelongs to the\nara::per::PerErrorDomain\n, which can be\nused by an\napplication\nto classify returned errors.\n[SWS_PER_00473]\nd\nara::per::GetPerDomain\nshall return the global\nara::\nper::PerErrorDomain\nobject.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nTo create its own\nPersistency\nerror codes, the\napplication\nmay use\nara::\nper::MakeErrorCode\n.\n[SWS_PER_00474]\nd\nara::per::MakeErrorCode\nshall return an\nara::core::\nErrorCode\nwhen called with an error code from\nara::per::PerErrc\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_-\n00128)\n[SWS_PER_00353]\nd\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::Name\nshall return the NUL-\nterminated string Per.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00475]\nd\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::Message\nshall return the er-\nror message associated with the passed\nara::core::ErrorCode\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe whole\nPersistency\nAPI has been designed to be exception-less. If an\nap-\nplication\nprefers to use exceptions, it may use\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::\nThrowAsException\n, or simply\nara::core::ErrorCode::ThrowAsException\n.\n[SWS_PER_00476]\nd\nara::per::PerErrorDomain::ThrowAsException\nshall\nthrow an\nara::per::PerException\nthat is created from the passed error code.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00571]\nd\nWhen\nPersistency\ndetects an inconsistency in the\nmanifest\nincluding invalid or non-existing URIs, it shall treat this situation as a violation as defined\nin [2] and call\nara::core::Abort\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00149)\n7.2.2.1 Handling of General Errors\n[SWS_PER_00536]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\nencounters a prob-\nlem with the hardware or the underlaying operating system services during the access\nto a\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkPhysicalStorageFailure\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n37 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P38_117",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00537",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 38,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nWhen\nkPhysicalStorageFailure\noccurs, the\napplication\ncannot access the\naffected\nstorage\nany more. Depending on the system, a reboot might restore the\naccess.\n[SWS_PER_00537]\nd\nWhen a method of\nPersistency\nwould modify the underlying\nstorage\n, but the\nstorage\nis configured as read-only (the\nPortPrototype\nthat is\ntyped by the corresponding\nPersistencyInterface\nis instantiated as\nRPortPro-\ntotype\n),\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkIllegalWriteAccess\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_-\n00128)\n[SWS_PER_00538]\nd\nWhen a function of\nPersistency\nis called with an\nara::\ncore::InstanceSpecifier\nthat is not available in the\nmanifest\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkStorageNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe two previous errors (\nkIllegalWriteAccess\nand\nkStorageNotFound\n) occur\nwhen the configuration does not match the implemented access to a\nstorage\n. An\napplication\nmight be implemented to be aware of this possibility and react accord-\ningly to the error by avoiding (write) accesses to the\nstorage\n. If the\napplication\ndepends on (write) access to the\nstorage\n, these errors would hint at an incorrect\nconfiguration of the\nstorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00539]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\ndetects a funda-\nmental problem in the structure of the\nstorage\nthat prevents accessing the\nstorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkIntegrityCorrupted\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe\napplication\ncan restore a corrupted\nstorage\nby calling\nara::per::Recov-\nerKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::Re-\ncoverAllFiles\n, or\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\n. When the\nkIntegrityCor-\nrupted\nis reported for an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\n,\nintegrity\ncan be restored\nby calling\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\n,\nara::per::KeyVal-\nueStorage::ResetKey\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\n, or\nara::\nper::FileStorage::ResetFile\n.\nWhen\nPersistency\ndetects insufficient or broken redundancy, it will report\nkVali-\ndationFailed\nas described in [SWS_PER_00221].\n[SWS_PER_00540]\nd\nWhen encryption or decryption of\npersistent data\nfails\nwithin a function or method of\nPersistency\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkEncryptionFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00564]\nd\nWhen the calculation or verification of the\nMAC\nof\npersistent\ndata\nfails within a function or method of\nPersistency\n,\nPersistency\nshall return\nthe error\nkAuthenticationFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThe two previous errors can occur when the configured cryptographic keys or algo-\nrithms are not available at run time, or when the\nstorage\nor the\nelement\nof a\nstor-\nage\nis corrupted. The latter case could be detected or even avoided by configuring\nredundancy\n.\n38 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P39_118",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00541",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 39,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00541]\nd\nWhen a method of\nPersistency\ntries to read data from a\nfile\n,\nbut the position is already at the end,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkIsEof\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error can typically be dealt with by the\napplication\n, and can be avoided by\nusing\nara::per::ReadAccessor::IsEof\n.\n[SWS_PER_00542]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\nwould create a\nfile\n, but the number of existing\nfiles\nalready equals the configured\nPersistency-\nFileStorageInterface\n.\nmaxNumberOfFiles\nof the corresponding\nFile Stor-\nage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkTooManyFiles\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error might occur when a new\nfile\nis opened for writing, or when a\nFile Stor-\nage\nis updated or when it is recovered after an error. An\napplication\nseeing this\nerror might delete some\nfiles\nto be able to create the new\nfile\n(or\nfiles\n), or reset\nthe\nFile Storage\nto the initial state using\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\nor\nara::\nper::ResetPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00543]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\nwould increase the\nsize of a\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\nsuch that the total storage size would\nexceed the configured\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\nof the\nstorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkQuotaExceeded\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error means that the\napplication\ntried to store data that exceeds the\nconfigured quota of a\nstorage\n. The\napplication\nhas to be able to deal\nwith this situation, and either write less data to the affected\nstorage\nor re-\nmove outdated data from this\nstorage\n, or reset the affected\nelement\n/\nstor-\nage\nwith a call to\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::ResetAll-\nFiles\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::ResetKey\n,\nara::per::FileStor-\nage::ResetFile\n, or even\nara::per::ResetPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00544]\nd\nWhen a function or method of\nPersistency\ncannot increase\nthe size of a\nstorage\nbecause the\nphysical storage\nis not sufficient (e.g. file\nsystem quoata exceeded or partition full),\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkOut-\nOfStorageSpace\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis error means that some other\nstorage\nor even a completely independent process\noccupies so much\nphysical storage\nthat\nPersistency\ncannot store additional\ndata. This can only happen if\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\nis\nconfigured to a higher value than\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nminimumSustained-\nSize\n. The\napplication\nhas to be able to deal with this situation, and either write less\ndata to the affected\nstorage\nor remove outdated data from this or another\nstorage\n,\nor reset this or another\nelement\n/\nstorage\nwith a call to\nara::per::ResetKeyVal-\nueStorage\n,\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::\nResetKey\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\n, or even\nara::per::Re-\nsetPersistency\n.\n39 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P40_119",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00309",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 40,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.3 Parallel Access to Persistent Data\nAccording to [8], the\npersistent data\nis local to one\nProcess\n. Therefore,\nPer-\nsistency\nwill never share\npersistent data\nbetween two (or more)\nProcess\nes,\neven of the same\nExecutable\n. The background of this decision is that\nPersistency\nshould not provide an additional communication path for\napplications\nbesides the\nmechanisms provided by the\nfunctional cluster\nCommunication Management\n(e.g. using ara::com).\n[SWS_PER_00309]\nd\nPersistent data\nshall always be local to one\nProcess\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nIf\npersistent data\nneeds to be accessed by multiple\nProcess\nes (of the same or\ndifferent\napplications\n), it is the duty of the application designer to provide\nService\nInterfaces\nfor communication.\nPersistency\nis, on the other hand, prepared to handle concurrent access from mul-\ntiple threads of the same\napplication\n, running in the context of the same\nProcess\n.\nTo create shared access to a\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n, either the\nara::per::SharedHandle\nreturned by\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nand\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\ncan be passed on (i.e. copied) to another thread, or\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nand\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\ncan be\ncalled in independent threads for the same\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n,\nrespectively. All operations of the\nKey-Value Storage\nand\nFile Storage\nsupport\nconcurrent access from multiple threads, though operations like\nara::per::Recov-\nerKeyValueStorage\nand\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\nor\nara::per::\nRecoverAllFiles\nand\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\nwill only succeed when the\ncorresponding\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nis not opened.\n[SWS_PER_00545]\nd\nWhen a function of\nPersistency\nthat modifies a\nstorage\nis\ncalled while another function that modifies the same\nstorage\nis being executed,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkResourceBusy\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\nThis restriction also applies to global functions like\nara::per::UpdatePersis-\ntency\n, which will only succeed if no\nstorage\nis open, and no other thread is currently\nmodifying a\nstorage\nwith functions like\nara::per::RecoverKeyValueStorage\nor\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\n.\nAccess to single\nkey-value pairs\nof a\nKey-Value Storage\nis possi-\nble from multiple threads at the same time, because the operation of\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nand\nara::per::KeyValueStor-\nage::SetValue\nare atomic, as are those of\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::Re-\nmoveKey\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveAllKeys\n,\nara::per::Key-\nValueStorage::SyncToStorage\n, and\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::Dis-\ncardPendingChanges\n.\nAccess to single\nfiles\nof a\nFile Storage\ncannot be shared between multiple\nthreads, because it would be impossible to synchronize read and write accesses and\nthe corresponding change of the seek position in a\nfile\n. Accordingly, the\nara::\n40 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nper::UniqueHandle\nreturned by the\nOpenFile\n*\nAPIs can only be moved to an-\nother thread, and trying to open an already opened\nfile\nwill fail. Likewise, operations\nlike\nara::per::FileStorage::DeleteFile\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::Re-\ncoverFile\n, and\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\nwill also not be possible\non open\nfiles\n.\n[SWS_PER_00546]\nd\nWhen a method of\nara::per::FileStorage\nthat opens or\nmodifies a\nfile\nis called while the same\nfile\nis currently open or being modified\nby another method,\nPersistency\nshall return the error\nkResourceBusy\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_-\n00128)\nFiles\nare implicitly closed when their\nara::per::UniqueHandle\ngoes out of\nscope, or when the\nFile Storage\nto which they belong is closed.\n[SWS_PER_00425]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nis closed, because all related\nara::\nper::SharedHandle\ns go out of scope, any\nfiles\nwhich are still open are also\nclosed.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nAccessing a\nara::per::UniqueHandle\nof a\nfile\nof a closed\nFile Storage\nwill\nresult in undefined behavior.\n41 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P42_121",
