      "source_page": 42,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.4 Security Concepts\nThe\nPersistency\nsupports protection of the authenticity and confidentiality of data\nstored in a\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n. Which kind of protection is\napplied and the used algorithms are decided at deployment time. The\napplication\nis not aware of this fact.\nIf confidentiality of data shall be protected, a\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof a\nstorage\nare encrypted after the creation of the\nstorage\nand when the\nstorage\nis saved, and\nare decrypted when a\nstorage\nis opened. Therefore, only encrypted data is stored\npersistently. In case of a read-only\nstorage\n, encryption is done only once during\ninstallation, decryption is done every time the\nstorage\nis opened.\nIf authenticity of data shall be protected, a message authentication code (\nMAC\n) is gen-\nerated after the creation of a\nstorage\nand when the\nstorage\nis saved, and verified\nwhen the\nstorage\nis opened. Therefore, unauthorized modifications to the\nstorage\ncan be detected.\nIn case of a read-only\nstorage\n, it is also possible to protect the authenticity of the\nstorage\n(or an\nelement\ntherein) by calculating a hash value of the data to be pro-\ntected and comparing this calculated value to a hash value provided in the\nmanifest\n.\nThis assumes that the authenticity of the processed manifest is protected using other\nmechanisms (like secure boot).\nIf authenticity and confidentiality shall be protected, authenticated encryption schemes\n(like AES GCM) can be used.\n[SWS_PER_00210]\nd\nIf a\nPersistencyDeploymentToCryptoKeySlotMapping\nexists in the\nmanifest\n, and\nPersistencyDeploymentToCryptoKeySlot-\nMapping\n.\nkeySlotUsage\nis set to\nencryption\n, the\nPersistency\nshall encrypt\nall data related to the\nstorage\nusing the algorithm specified by\nPersistency-\nDeploymentToCryptoKeySlotMapping\n.\ncryptoAlgorithmString\nbefore stor-\ning it to the persistent memory.\nc\n(RS_PER_00005, RS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00464]\nd\nIf a\nPersistencyDeploymentElementToCryptoKeySlot-\nMapping\nexists in the\nmanifest\n, and\nPersistencyDeploymentElementTo-\nCryptoKeySlotMapping\n.\nkeySlotUsage\nis set to\nencryption\n, the\nPersistency\nshall encrypt the\nelement\ndata using the algorithm specified by\nPersistency-\nDeploymentElementToCryptoKeySlotMapping\n.\ncryptoAlgorithmString\nbe-\nfore storing it to the persistent memory.\nc\n(RS_PER_00005, RS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00211]\nd\nIf a\nPersistencyDeploymentToCryptoKeySlotMapping\nexists in the\nmanifest\n, and\nPersistencyDeploymentToCryptoKeySlot-\nMapping\n.\nkeySlotUsage\nis set to\nencryption\n, the\nPersistency\nshall decrypt\nall data related to the\nstorage\nusing the algorithm specified by\nPersistency-\nDeploymentToCryptoKeySlotMapping\n.\ncryptoAlgorithmString\nafter reading\nit from persistent memory.\nc\n(RS_PER_00005, RS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00465]\nd\nIf a\nPersistencyDeploymentElementToCryptoKeySlot-\nMapping\nexists in the\nmanifest\n, and\nPersistencyDeploymentElementTo-\n42 of 196       "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nElementToCryptoKeySlotMapping\n.\nverificationHash\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00019,\nRS_PER_00010)\nThe\nPersistency\nwill use the services of the\nCryptography\n[9] for all cryptographic\noperations.\n44 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P45_124",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00317",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 45,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.5 Redundancy Concepts\nThe\nPersistency\nshall take care of the integrity of the stored data, both for safety\npurposes and to prevent data loss. This can be achieved by calculating CRCs or hash\nvalues of the stored data, and by creating redundant copies. All these measures ef-\nfectively create some\nredundancy\nfor the stored data. The concrete measures to be\ntaken are configurable: The application designer can use\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nredundancy\nto request\nredundancy\n(by setting it to\nredundant\nor\nredundant-\nPerElement\n), or use\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nredundancyHandling\nto prese-\nlect the actual measures to be taken. During deployment, the integrator can define the\nactual measures taken to ensure data integrity using\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nre-\ndundancyHandling\n. If\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis con-\nfigured, the integrator shall use it as a guidance, but may also choose other, more\nappropriate measures based on superior knowledge of the final system.\n[SWS_PER_00317]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall store redundant information for ev-\nery\nstorage\nrepresented by a\nPersistencyDeployment\nwhere\nPersisten-\ncyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis configured.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_-\n00009, RS_PER_00010)\nThe actual handling of the\nredundancy\nconfigured during deployment is described\nin the following sections, see also [SWS_PER_00318], [SWS_PER_00319], and\n[SWS_PER_00447].\n[SWS_PER_00221]\nd\nPersistency\nshall check the redundant data when accessing\nstored data. When the stored data is corrupted,\nPersistency\nshall try to restore it\nusing the available\nredundancy\n. If\nPersistency\nis not able to recover using the\nredundancy\n, it shall report\nkValidationFailed\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\nDepending on the actual implementation,\nPersistency\nmight access the stored data\nat different times, e.g. when\nara::core::Initialize\nis called, when a\nKey-\n-Value Storage\nis opened, or when a\nfile\nis accessed. The question whether\nthe\nredundancy\nis sufficient for recovery is also implementation specific and can only\nbe safely assumed for\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\n.\nWhen the recovery failed, the\napplication\ncan choose to use\nara::per::Recov-\nerKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\n,\nara::\nper::RecoverAllFiles\n, or\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\nto re-\ncover as much as possible and set the corresponding\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile\nStorage\nagain into a consistent state.\n[SWS_PER_00452]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::RecoverKeyValueStorage\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall restore the\nKey-Value Storage\nto a consistent state, including\nredundancy\n. First, the infrastructure of the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nshall be re-\nstored, then\nPersistency\nshall try to recover all\nkey-value pairs\navailable in the\nKey-Value Storage\nas described in [SWS_PER_00453]. Depending on available\ninformation, the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nmight be reset to the initial state as de-\nscribed in [SWS_PER_00456], losing all updated\nvalues\nof its\nkey-value pairs\n,\nor may contain outdated\nkey-value pairs\nafter the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\n45 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P46_125",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00547",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 46,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00547]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present\nin any instance of the\nKey-Value Storage\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00453]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RecoverKey\nis\ncalled for an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall try to restore the\ngiven\nkey\nto a consistent state, including\nredundancy\n. Depending on available\ninformation, the\nkey\nmight be removed, reset to the initial\nvalue\nas described\nin [SWS_PER_00477], or might contain an outdated\nvalue\nafter the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\n[SWS_PER_00454]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::RecoverAllFiles\nis called,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall restore the\nFile Storage\nto a consistent state, including\nredundancy\n.\nFirst, the infrastructure of the whole\nFile Storage\nshall be restored as described\nin [SWS_PER_00478], then\nPersistency\nshall try to recover all currently available\nfiles\nas described in [SWS_PER_00455]. Depending on available information, the\nwhole\nFile Storage\nmight be reset to the initial state, losing all updated content of\nits\nfiles\n, or may contain outdated\nfiles\nafter the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\n[SWS_PER_00548]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n,\nand otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00455]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::RecoverFile\nis called for\nan existing\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall try to restore the given\nfile\nto a consistent\nstate, including\nredundancy\n. Depending on available information, the\nfile\nmight be\nremoved, reset to the initial state as described in [SWS_PER_00479], or might contain\noutdated content after the operation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009)\nOf course the\napplication\nhas to validate the restored data in this case.\nOr it can use\nara::per::ResetPersistency\n(see [SWS_PER_00556]),\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\n(see [SWS_PER_00456]),\nara::per::\nKeyValueStorage::ResetKey\n(see [SWS_PER_00477]),\nara::per::Rese-\ntAllFiles\n(see [SWS_PER_00478]), or\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\n(see [SWS_PER_00479]) to reset the corrupted item to the initial state according to\nthe current\nmanifest\n.\nThe\napplication\nmay want to monitor its\nstorages\nfor any problem detected by\nredundancy\n, even if\nPersistency\nis able to recover by itself. This might be required\nto e.g. get an early indication of hardware problems or for safety critical\napplica-\ntions\n. This monitoring is supported by\nPersistency\n, which will trigger a callback\nfunction of the\napplication\nin case of any problems with the\nstorages\n. To activate\nthis monitoring, the\napplication\nhas to register that callback function using\nara::\nper::RegisterRecoveryReportCallback\n.\n[SWS_PER_00480]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::RegisterRecoveryReportCallback\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall register the provided function and enable reporting of\nredundancy\nproblems in all\nstorages\nof this\napplication\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n46 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P47_126",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00481",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 47,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nPersistency\nmay check\nredundancy\nat different places, e.g. when\nara::core::\nInitialize\nis called, when a\nstorage\nis opened, or when\nelements\nof the\nstorage\nare accessed. Whenever a problem is detected with\nredundancy\n, inde-\npendently of the situation in which the problem appeared or whether the problem\ncould be handled,\nPersistency\nwill inform the\napplication\nabout these problems\nvia the registered callback, stating\nkKeyValueStorageRecovered\n,\nkKeyRecov-\nered\n,\nkFileStorageRecovered\n, or\nkFileRecovered\nwhen recovery of a\nKey-\n-Value Storage\n, a\nFile Storage\n, a\nkey-value pair\n, or a\nfile\nwas possible,\nand\nkKeyValueStorageRecoveryFailed\n,\nkKeyRecoveryFailed\n,\nkFileStor-\nageRecoveryFailed\n, or\nkFileRecoveryFailed\nif not. The callback also reports\nthe affected\nstorage\n, the affected\nelements\n, and how many copies of these\nele-\nments\nwere affected (the latter only in case\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\nis\nconfigured).\n[SWS_PER_00481]\nd\nWhen a\nKey-Value Storage\nis accessed, and a\nredun-\ndancy\nproblem affecting the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nis detected that cannot be\nhandled by\nPersistency\n(i.e.\nkValidationFailed\nis returned),\nPersistency\nshall call the registered callback with\nstorage\nset to the\nara::core::Instance-\nSpecifier\nof the\nKey-Value Storage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkKeyVal-\nueStorageRecoveryFailed\n, an empty\nara::core::Vector\nfor\nreportedEle-\nments\n, and an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant in-\nstances of the\nKey-Value Storage\nin\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00482]\nd\nWhen a\nKey-Value Storage\nis accessed, and a\nredun-\ndancy\nproblem affecting the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nis detected that can be\nhandled by\nPersistency\n(i.e. the operation succeeds),\nPersistency\nshall call the\nregistered callback with\nstorage\nset to the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nof\nthe\nKey-Value Storage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkKeyValueStorageRe-\ncovered\n, an empty\nara::core::Vector\nfor\nreportedElements\n, and an\nara::\ncore::Vector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant instances of the\nKey-\n-Value Storage\nin\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00483]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nis reg-\nistered callback with\nstorage\nset to the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nof the\nFile Storage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkFileStorageRecoveryFailed\n,\nan empty\nara::core::Vector\nfor\nreportedElements\n, and an\nara::core::\nVector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant instances of the\nFile AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nthe affected redundant instances of the\nFile Storage\nin\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00485]\nd\nWhen a\nKey-Value Storage\nor one of its\nkeys\nis accessed,\nand a\nredundancy\nproblem affecting a set of\nkeys\nis detected that cannot be han-\ndled by\nPersistency\n(i.e.\nkValidationFailed\nis returned),\nPersistency\nshall\ncall the registered callback with storage set to the\nara::core::InstanceSpeci-\nfier\nof the\nKey-Value Storage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkKeyRecovery-\nFailed\n, an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the affected\nkeys\nin\nreportedElements\n,\nand an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant instances of\nthe\nkeys\nin\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00486]\nd\nWhen a\nKey-Value Storage\nor one of its\nkeys\nis accessed,\nand a\nredundancy\nproblem affecting a set of\nkeys\nis detected that can be han-\ndled by\nPersistency\n(i.e. the operation succeeds),\nPersistency\nshall call the\nregistered callback with\nstorage\nset to the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nof the\nKey-Value Storage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkKeyRecovered\n, an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the affected\nkeys\nin\nreportedElements\n, and an\nara::\ncore::Vector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant instances of the\nkeys\nin\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00487]\nd\nWhen a\nredundancy\nproblem of single\nkeys\nis reported ac-\ncording to [SWS_PER_00485] or [SWS_PER_00486],\nPersistency\nshall in general\nensure that each entry in\nreportedElements\nmatches an entry in\nreportedIn-\nstances\nat the same positions, the two\nara::core::Vector\ns shall have the same\nsize. If several instances of a\nkey\nare affected, the\nkey\nmay appear several times\nin\nreportedElements\n. As an optimization, if only one\nkey\nis affected,\nreport-\nedElements\nmay contain the affected\nkey\nas single entry, related to all entries of\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00488]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nor one of its\nfiles\nis accessed, and\na\nredundancy\nproblem affecting a set of\nfiles\nis detected that cannot be han-\ndled by\nPersistency\n(i.e.\nkValidationFailed\nis returned),\nPersistency\nshall\ncall the registered callback with\nstorage\nset to the\nara::core::InstanceSpec-\nifier\nof the\nFile Storage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkFileRecovery-\nFailed\n, an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the affected\nfiles\nin\nreportedElements\n,\nand an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant instances of\nthe\nfiles\nin\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n[SWS_PER_00489]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nor one of its\nfiles\nis accessed, and\na\nredundancy\nproblem affecting a set of\nfiles\nis detected that can be handled by\nPersistency\n(i.e. the operation succeeds),\nPersistency\nshall call the registered\ncallback with\nstorage\nset to the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nof the\nFile\nStorage\n,\nrecoveryReportKind\nset to\nkFileRecovered\n, an\nara::core::Vec-\ntor\nwith the affected\nfiles\nin\nreportedElements\n, and an\nara::core::Vector\nwith the indices of the affected redundant instances of the\nfiles\nin\nreportedIn-\nstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n48 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P49_128",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00490",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 49,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00490]\nd\nWhen a\nredundancy\nproblem of single\nfile\nis reported ac-\ncording to [SWS_PER_00488] or [SWS_PER_00489],\nPersistency\nshall in general\nensure that each entry in\nreportedElements\nmatches an entry in\nreportedIn-\nstances\nat the same positions, the two\nara::core::Vector\ns shall have the same\nsize. If several instances of a\nfile\nare affected, the\nfile\nmay appear several times\nin\nreportedElements\n. As an optimization, if only one\nfile\nis affected,\nreport-\nedElements\nmay contain the affected\nfile\nas single entry, related to all entries of\nreportedInstances\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008)\n7.2.5.1 Redundancy Types\nThe type of\nredundancy\nthat is applied by the\nPersistency\nis defined by the set\nof\nPersistencyRedundancyHandling\nclasses aggregated as\nPersistencyDe-\nployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\n. The level to which\nredundancy\nis applied is de-\nfined by the possible values of the\nPersistencyRedundancyHandlingScopeEnum\n,\nwhich are\npersistencyRedundancyHandlingScopeStorage\nand\npersisten-\ncyRedundancyHandlingScopeElement\nfor a\nKey-Value Storage\nand its\nkey-\n-value pairs\n, or a\nFile Storage\nand its\nfiles\n, respectively.\n[SWS_PER_00318]\nd\nIn case a\nPersistencyRedundancyHandling\naggregated\nas\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis derived as\nPersisten-\ncyRedundancyCrc\n, the\nPersistency\nshall calculate a CRC value when persisting\nthe\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof the\nstorage\n(depending on\nPersistencyDeploy-\nment\n.\nredundancyHandling\n.\nscope\n), and shall use this CRC to check the\nstorage\nor the\nelement\nwhen it is read back.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_-\n00010)\n[SWS_PER_00439]\nd\nPersistency\nshall calculate the CRC value using the al-\ngorithm defined by\nPersistencyRedundancyCrc\n.\nalgorithmFamily\nwith the bit\nwidth defined by\nPersistencyRedundancyCrc\n.\nlength\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_-\nPER_00009, RS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00319]\nd\nIn case a\nPersistencyRedundancyHandling\naggregated\nas\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis derived as\nPersisten-\ncyRedundancyMOutOfN\n, the\nPersistency\nshall store N copies when persisting the\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof the\nstorage\n(depending on\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\n.\nscope\n), and shall check that at least M of the N copies of the\nstorage\nor the\nelement\nare identical when it is read back. N is defined by\nn\n, and M\nis defined by\nm\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010)\nIt is possible to configure more than one\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\ndeploymen-\ntUri\nfor a\nstorage\nthat uses\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\n. In this case, the\ncopies will be distributed over the different locations. The existence of multiple URIs\nfor a single\nstorage\nis limited to this case by [constr_10366].\n[SWS_PER_00555]\nd\nIn case multiple\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\ndeploymentUri\ns\nexist, and\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\n.\nscope\nis\npersis-\n49 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P50_129",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00447",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 50,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\ntencyRedundancyHandlingScopeStorage\n,\nPersistency\nshall store the copies\nof the\nstorage\nin the different locations as follows:\n2\nThe first location contains the main copy, the second location contains all other\ncopies.\nn\n(==\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\n.\nn\n) Each copy is placed in a separate lo-\ncation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00447]\nd\nIn case a\nPersistencyRedundancyHandling\naggregated\nas\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nredundancyHandling\nis derived as\nPersisten-\ncyRedundancyHash\n, the\nPersistency\nshall calculate a hash value when persisting\nthe\nstorage\nor an\nelement\nof the\nstorage\n(depending on\nPersistencyDeploy-\nment\n.\nredundancyHandling\n.\nscope\n), and shall use this hash value to check the\nstorage\nor the\nelement\nwhen it is read back.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009,\nRS_PER_00010)\n[SWS_PER_00448]\nd\nPersistency\nshall calculate the hash value using the algo-\nrithm defined by\nPersistencyRedundancyHash\n.\nalgorithmFamily\nwith the bit\nwidth defined by\nPersistencyRedundancyHash\n.\nlength\n. If\nPersistencyRedun-\ndancyHash\n.\ninitializationVectorLength\nis configured, an initialization vector\nof this length shall be calculated containing random data and passed to the hash algo-\nrithm.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010)\nA possible approach to calculate the hash value and the random data would be to\nuse the\nCryptography\n[9]. The integration will have to take care that the con-\nfigured\nPersistencyRedundancyHash\n.\nlength\nand\nPersistencyRedundancy-\nHash\n.\ninitializationVectorLength\nare supported by the configured\nPersis-\ntencyRedundancyHash\n.\nalgorithmFamily\n.\n50 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P51_130",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00463",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 51,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.6 Installation and Update of Persistent Data\nThe\nUpdate and Configuration Management\n[7] handles the life cycle of\nAdap-\ntive Applications\nwith the following phases:\n\u000f\nInstallation of new software\n\u000f\nUpdate of already installed software\n\u000f\nFinalization of updated software after the update succeeded\n\u000f\nRoll-back of updated software after the update failed\n\u000f\nRemoval of installed software\nFor all these phases,\npersistent data\nneeds to be handled alongside the appli-\ncation. The\nAdaptive Application\nmay trigger this handling explicitly by calling\nara::per::UpdatePersistency\nduring the verification phase that follows the in-\nstallation or update, or rely on the\nPersistency\nto do this implicitly when\nper-\nsistent data\nis accessed (\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n/\nara::per::\nOpenFileStorage\n). In both cases, the\nPersistency\nwill compare a previously\nstored\ncontract version\nand\ndeployment version\nagainst the\ncontract\nversion\nand\ndeployment version\nof the current\nmanifest\n, and perform the re-\nquired action.\nPersistency\nstores information about already installed\nstorages\ntogether with ver-\nsion information in a central location.\n[SWS_PER_00463]\nd\nPersistency\nshall store information about the installed\nKey-Value Storages\nand\nFile Storages\nin the location denoted by\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersistencyCentralStorageURI\nof the\nPro-\ncessToMachineMapping\nthat refers to the\nProcess\nthat is referenced by\nPersis-\ntencyPortPrototypeToDeploymentMapping\ns. It shall also store the\ncontract\nversion\nand\ndeployment version\nof the current\nmanifest\nin this location.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014, RS_PER_00016)\n[SWS_PER_00469]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::UpdatePersistency\nis called, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall follow [SWS_PER_00382] (for installation), [SWS_PER_00386] and\n[SWS_PER_00387] (for update), or [SWS_PER_00396] (for roll-back) for each\nstor-\nage\nconfigured as\nPersistencyDeployment\nin the deployment data.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014)\n[SWS_PER_00470]\nd\nWhen a\nKey-Value Storage\nis opened by the applica-\ntion using\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n, the\nPersistency\nshall follow\n[SWS_PER_00382] (for installation), [SWS_PER_00386] and [SWS_PER_00387] (for\nupdate), [SWS_PER_00446] (for finalization), or [SWS_PER_00396] (for roll-back) for\nthis\nKey-Value Storage\nconfigured as\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nin the\ndeployment data.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_-\n00014, RS_PER_00016)\n51 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P52_131",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00471",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 52,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00471]\nd\nWhen a\nFile Storage\nis opened by the\napplica-\ntion\nusing\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\n, the\nPersistency\nshall follow\n[SWS_PER_00382] (for installation), [SWS_PER_00386] and [SWS_PER_00387] (for\nupdate), [SWS_PER_00446] (for finalization), or [SWS_PER_00396] (for roll-back) for\neach\nFile Storage\nconfigured as\nPersistencyFileStorage\nin the deployment\ndata.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014, RS_-\nPER_00016)\n[SWS_PER_00378]\nd\nPersistency\nshall extract the\ncontract version\n(\nPersis-\ntencyInterface\n.\ncontractVersion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWith-\nPersistencyDeploymentMapping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) and the\ndeployment\nversion\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) from the\nmanifest\n, and store\nthem persistently in the location denoted by\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersis-\ntencyCentralStorageURI\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013, RS_PER_00014)\nThe\ncontract version\nis used by\nPersistency\nto detect a change of the ap-\nplication (see [SWS_PER_00387]), while the\ndeployment version\nis used to de-\ntect a change of the deployed\npersistent data\n(see [SWS_PER_00386] and\n[SWS_PER_00396]).\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00001]\nd\nWhen the\ncontract version\n(\nPersistencyIn-\nterface\n.\ncontractVersion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersis-\ntencyDeploymentMapping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) is increased, the\ndeployment\nversion\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) needs to be increased, too.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nThe\ndeployment version\nand\ncontract version\nare\nStrongRevisionLa-\nbelString\ns. These strings consists of a\nMajorVersion\n, a\nMinorVersion\n, a\nPatchVersion\n, and additional labels for pre-release versions and build information.\nIt is assumed that at least one of the first three will be incremented when the version is\nchanged, while the additional labels might be arbitrary.\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00002]\nd\nWhen the\ndeployment version\n(\nPersistency-\nDeployment\n.\nversion\n) or\ncontract version\n(\nPersistencyInterface\n.\ncon-\ntractVersion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploy-\nmentMapping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) is increased, the\nMajorVersion\n,\nMinorVer-\nsion\n, or\nPatchVersion\nhave to be incremented.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_-\n00012)\nAfter installation of the\nAdaptive Application\n, the\nPersistency\nwill install pre-\ndefined\npersistent data\nfrom the\nmanifest\n. There are different possibilities how\nthis\npersistent data\ncan be defined in the\nmanifest\n:\n\u000f\nPersistent data\ncan be defined by an application designer within\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nor\nPersistencyFileStor-\nageInterface\n.\n\u000f\nPersistent data\nthat was defined by an application designer can be changed\nand fine-tuned by an integrator within\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nor\nPersistencyFileStorage\n.\n52 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P53_132",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00379",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 53,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n\u000f\nPersistent data\ncan be directly defined by an integrator within\nPersisten-\ncyKeyValueStorage\nor\nPersistencyFileStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00379]\nd\nElements\ndefined in the deployment data (\nPersistencyDe-\nploymentElement\n) shall always be preferred over the\nelements\ndefined in the ap-\nplication design (\nPersistencyInterfaceElement\n). The latter shall only be used if\nthe former does not exist.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013)\nAfter an update of the\nAdaptive Application\nor the\nmanifest\n, the\nPersis-\ntency\nwill create a backup of the\npersistent data\n, and then update the existing\npersistent data\nusing one of the following strategies:\n\u000f\nExisting\npersistent data\nis kept unchanged (\nkeepExisting\n).\n\u000f\nExisting\npersistent data\nis replaced (\noverwrite\n).\n\u000f\nExisting\npersistent data\nis removed (\ndelete\n).\n\u000f\nNew\npersistent data\nis added (\nkeepExisting\nand\noverwrite\n).\nThe update strategy can be set during application design or deployment, and can\nbe defined for the whole\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\n(\nPersistency-\nCollectionLevelUpdateStrategyEnum\n\nkeepExisting\nor\ndelete\n) and for a\nsingle\nkey-value pair\nor\nfile\n(\nPersistencyElementLevelUpdateStrate-\ngyEnum\n\nkeepExisting\n,\noverwrite\n, or\ndelete\n).\n[SWS_PER_00251]\nd\nAn update strategy defined in the deployment data (\nPersis-\ntencyDeploymentElement\n.\nupdateStrategy\n) shall always be preferred over the\nupdate strategy defined in the application design (\nPersistencyInterfaceEle-\nment\n.\nupdateStrategy\n). The latter shall only be used if the former does not exist.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013)\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nupdateStrategy\nis a mandatory attribute and therefore\nPersistencyInterface\n.\nupdateStrategy\nis just a recommendation for the de-\nployment and never used by\nPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00380]\nd\nAn update strategy defined for a single\nelement\n(\nPersisten-\ncyDeploymentElement\n.\nupdateStrategy\n,\nPersistencyInterfaceElement\n.\nupdateStrategy\n) shall always be preferred over the update strategy defined for\nthe enclosing\nstorage\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nupdateStrategy\n,\nPersis-\ntencyInterface\n.\nupdateStrategy\n). The latter shall only be used if the former\ndoes not exist.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012, RS_PER_00013)\nWhen the update succeeded, the\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nwill\nfinalize the new\nAdaptive Application\n. The\nPersistency\nwill free the resources\nallocated by the last backup when it is opened the first time after the update succeeded.\nWhen the update failed, the\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nwill revert\nto the old\nAdaptive Application\nand/or\nmanifest\n. The\nPersistency\nwill then\nreplace the currently used\npersistent data\nby the backup created during the up-\ndate.\n53 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P54_133",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00556",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 54,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe application can always reset its\nstorages\nor single\nelements\nof the\nstor-\nages\nto their initial state, using\nara::per::ResetPersistency\n,\nara::per::\nResetKeyValueStorage\n,\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::ResetKey\n,\nara::\nper::ResetAllFiles\n, or\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\n.\n[SWS_PER_00556]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::ResetPersistency\nis called,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall reset all\nKey-Value Storages\nand\nFile Storages\nto the state they\nwould have after installation of the\napplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninfor-\nmation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00456]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\nis called,\nPer-\nsistency\nshall reset the\nKey-Value Storage\nto the state it would have after in-\nstallation of the\napplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00572]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::ResetKey\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present in the\nman-\nifest\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkInitValueNotAvailable\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00477]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::ResetKey\nis called\nfor a\nkey-value pair\nthat is present in the\nmanifest\n,\nPersistency\nshall reset\nthe given\nkey\nto the state it would have after installation of the\napplication\nusing the\ncurrent\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00478]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::ResetAllFiles\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall reset the\nFile Storage\nto the state it would have after installation of the\nap-\nplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00573]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nmanifest\n, and\notherwise return directly with\nkInitValueNotAvailable\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00479]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::ResetFile\nis called for a\nfile\nthat is present in the\nmanifest\n,\nPersistency\nshall reset the given\nfile\nto the\nstate it would have after installation of the\napplication\nusing the current\nmanifest\ninformation.\nc\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nFinally, when the\nAdaptive Application\nis removed, the\nUpdate and Config-\nuration Management\nis responsible to remove the related\npersistent data\nas\nwell.\n7.2.6.1 Installation of Persistent Data\n[SWS_PER_00382]\nd\nWhen a\nstorage\nis opened by the\napplication\n, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall check for the existence of any\npersistent data\nof this\nProcess\n.\n54 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P55_134",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00558",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 55,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIf no\npersistent data\nis found, the\nPersistency\nshall initialize the\npersistent\ndata\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nInitialization of\npersistent data\nis described in paragraph 7.2.6.1.1 and paragraph\n7.2.6.1.2.\nTo be able to update\nPersistency\nwith changed\nredundancy\n,\nPersistency\nstores\nthe information about the used\nredundancy\nmeasures within the\nmetadata\nof each\nstorage\n. The same applies to the used keys and algorithms for encryption and au-\nthentication.\n[SWS_PER_00558]\nd\nWhen a new\nstorage\nis installed,\nPersistency\nshall store the\ninformation about the used\nredundancy\nin the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00008, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00559]\nd\nWhen a new\nstorage\nis installed,\nPersistency\nshall store the\ninformation about keys and algorithms used for encryption and authentication in the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00005, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n7.2.6.1.1 Installation of Key-Value Storage\n[SWS_PER_00383]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create a\nKey-Value Storage\nfor each\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nthat is\nfound in the\nmanifest\nof a newly installed\nAdaptive Application\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012)\nThe\nKey-Value Storages\ncreated by [SWS_PER_00383] are identified at run-\ntime by the\nshortName\npath of the\nPortPrototype\n, passed as\nara::core::In-\nstanceSpecifier\nto\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00252]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create an entry in the\nKey-Value Stor-\nage\nfor each\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\n.\ndataElement\nand\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\n.\nkeyValuePair\nthat is found in the\nmanifest\nof\na newly installed or updated\nAdaptive Application\n, and for which the update\nstrategy is not\ndelete\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nKey-Value Storage\nentries are identified by the\nkey\n. An entry with identical\nkey\nmight be defined both in the\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\nas\ndataElement\nand the\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\nas\nkeyValuePair\n, in\nwhich case [SWS_PER_00379] applies. The update strategy is determined accord-\ning to [SWS_PER_00251] and [SWS_PER_00380].\n[SWS_PER_00253]\nd\nEntries in the\nKey-Value Storage\nshall use the\nshortName\nof the\nPersistencyDataElement\nand/or\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\nas\nkey\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00254]\nd\nEntries in the\nKey-Value Storage\nshall be created with\nthe data type defined by the\nCppImplementationDataType\nwhich types the\nPersistencyDataElement\nand/or by the\nCppImplementationDataType\nrefer-\n55 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P56_135",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00384",

      "source_page": 56,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nenced as\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\n.\nvalueDataType\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_-\nPER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00384]\nd\nEntries in the\nKey-Value Storage\nshall be created with the\nvalue taken from the\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\n.\ninitValue\nor, if that does\nnot exist, from the\nPersistencyDataRequiredComSpec\n.\ninitValue\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00003]\nd\nA\nmanifest\nis not valid if the value or data type of\nany\nPersistencyKeyValuePair\nor\nPersistencyDataElement\ncannot be deter-\nmined, or if the determined data types are conflicting.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_-\n00012)\nInvalid\nmanifests\nshould be rejected by the tooling.\n7.2.6.1.2 Installation of File Storage\n[SWS_PER_00385]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create a\nFile Storage\nfor each\nPort-\nPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface\nthat is found in the\nmanifest\nof a newly installed\nAdaptive Application\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_-\nPER_00012)\nThe\nFile Storages\ncreated by [SWS_PER_00385] are identified at run-time by the\nshortName\npath of the\nPortPrototype\n, passed as\nara::core::InstanceSpec-\nifier\nto\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00265]\nd\nPersistency\nshall create a\nfile\nin the\nFile Storage\nfor\neach\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface\n.\nfileElement\nand\nPersistency-\nFileStorage\n.\nfile\nthat is found in the\nmanifest\nof a newly installed or updated\nAdaptive Application\n, and for which the update strategy is not\ndelete\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nThe\nfiles\nwithin a\nFile Storage\nare identified by their\nfile name\n. A\nfile\nwith\nthe same\nfile name\nmight be defined both in the\nPersistencyFileStorageIn-\nterface\nas\nfileElement\nand the\nPersistencyFileStorage\nas\nfile\n, in which\ncase [SWS_PER_00379] applies. The update strategy is determined according to\n[SWS_PER_00251] and [SWS_PER_00380].\n[SWS_PER_00266]\nd\nFiles\nin the\nFile Storage\nshall use the\nfile name\niden-\ntified by\nPersistencyFileElement\n.\nfileName\nand/or\nPersistencyFile\n.\nfile-\nName\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n[SWS_PER_00267]\nd\nFiles\nin the\nFile Storage\nshall be created with the content\ntaken from the resource (within the installed\nSoftwarePackage\n) that is addressed\nby\nPersistencyFile\n.\ncontentUri\nor, if that does not exist, by\nPersistency-\nFileElement\n.\ncontentUri\n. If that does not exist either, an empty\nfile\nshall be\ncreated.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\n56 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P57_136",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_CONSTR_00004",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 57,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00004]\nd\nA\nmanifest\nis invalid if the\nshortName\ns of a\nPer-\nsistencyFileElement\nand a\nPersistencyFile\nwith the same\nfile name\ndif-\nfers.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00012)\nInvalid\nmanifests\nshould be rejected by the tooling.\n7.2.6.2 Update of Persistent Data\n[SWS_PER_00386]\nd\nWhen a\nstorage\nis opened by the\napplication\n, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall compare the\ndeployment version\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) in the\nmanifest\nagainst the stored\ndeployment version\n. If the\nde-\nployment version\nin the\nmanifest\nis higher than the stored\ndeployment ver-\nsion\n, the\nPersistency\nshall first create a backup of all the\npersistent data\nof\nthis\nProcess\nand then update the data.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\nOnly one set of backup data needs to be kept at any time. When a new update is\nperformed, old backup data could be overwritten. Update of\npersistent data\nis\ndescribed in paragraph 7.2.6.2.1 and paragraph 7.2.6.2.2.\n[SWS_PER_00387]\nd\nIf the\napplication\nregistered a function using\nara::per::\nRegisterApplicationDataUpdateCallback\n, and if the\nPersistency\nhad\nto update at least one of its\nstorages\naccording to [SWS_PER_00386], it\nshall compare the\ncontract version\n(\nPersistencyInterface\n.\ncontractVer-\nsion\nor\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMap-\nping\n.\ncontractVersion\n) in the\nmanifest\nagainst the stored\ncontract version\n.\nIf the\ncontract version\nin the\nmanifest\nis higher than the stored\ncontract\nversion\n, the\nPersistency\nshall call the registered function for each\nstorage\nthat\nwas updated according to [SWS_PER_00386].\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\nThe function registered by the\napplication\nusing\nara::per::RegisterAppli-\ncationDataUpdateCallback\ncan be used by the\napplication\nto update\nele-\nments\nof a\nstorage\nmanually. The\nstorage\nis identified by the\nara::core::In-\nstanceSpecifier\nprovided to this function. The\napplication\nmight then, based\non the\ncontract version\nof the stored data provided as second argument to the\nfunction, read in the stored data in the old format or with the old type, convert the data,\nand store it again with the new format or new type expected by the current\ncontract\nversion\n.\nExample: Version\n1\nof the\napplication\nstored the maximum speed in\nmph\nas\nuint8\n,\nbut version\n2\nexpects the maximum speed in\nkm=h\nas\nuint16\n. The update callback\nfunction will then see that a\nKey-Value Storage\nfrom version\n1\nof the\nPersistency\nhas been updated to the current version, and can read in the old maximum speed\nby\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nas\nuint8\n, convert it, and store it\nas\nuint16\nwith\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nafter removing the old\nvalue with\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\n.\n57 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P58_137",

      "source_page": 58,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nIn case the\nredundancy\nconfiguration or the configuration of encryption and authen-\ntication of the updated\nmanifest\ndiffers from the old\nmanifest\n, special care has to\nbe taken to keep the data consistent and readable.\n[SWS_PER_00560]\nd\nDuring the update, when the old\nstorage\nis read,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall check the\nredundancy\naccording to the information stored in the\nmeta-\ndata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\n[SWS_PER_00561]\nd\nWhen the\nstorage\nis persisted after the update,\nPersistency\nshall use the\nredundancy\nconfigured in the\nmanifest\n, and store the information\nabout the used\nredundancy\nin the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00008,\nRS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\nPlease note that this means that in some situations redundant information might be-\ncome obsolete and can be removed, e.g. when the new\nmanifest\nhas a lower\nn\nfor\nPersistencyRedundancyMOutOfN\n.\n[SWS_PER_00562]\nd\nDuring the update, when the old\nstorage\nis read,\nPersis-\ntency\nshall decrypt and verify the signature of the\nstorage\nor the\nelements\nof the\nstorage\naccording to the information stored in the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00005, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\n[SWS_PER_00563]\nd\nWhen the\nstorage\nis persisted after the update,\nPersistency\nshall encrypt and sign the\nstorage\nor the\nelements\nof the\nstorage\nas configured\nin the\nmanifest\n, and store the information about the used keys and algorithms in the\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00005, RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\n7.2.6.2.1 Update of Key-Value Storage\n[SWS_PER_00388]\nd\nWhen a new\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyKey-\nValueStorageInterface\nis detected in an updated\nmanifest\n, the\nPersistency\nshall create a\nKey-Value Storage\nas specified in [SWS_PER_00383].\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00010, RS_PER_00013)\n[SWS_PER_00389]\nd\nWhen a\nPortPrototype\ntyped by a\nPersistencyKeyVal-\nueStorageInterface\nis missing in an updated\nmanifest\n, a\nPersistencyKeyValueStorage\n.\nkeyValuePair\nwith a\nnew\nkey\nis detected in an updated\nmanifest\nfor which the\nupdate strategy\nis\nnot\ndelete\n, the\nPersistency\nshall create a new entry in the\nKey-Value Storage\nas specified in [SWS_PER_00252], [SWS_PER_00253], [SWS_PER_00254], and\n[SWS_PER_00384].\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\n[SWS_PER_00391]\nd\nWhen an existing\nkey-value pair\ncannot be associated with\nany\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\n.\ndataElement\nor\nPersisten-\ncyKeyValueStorage\n.\nkeyValuePair\nin an updated\nmanifest\n, and the update\n58 of 196 The update strategy is determined according to\n[SWS_PER_00251] and [SWS_PER_00380].\n[SWS_PER_00277]\nd\nWhen an existing\nkey-value pair\ncan be associated\nwith a\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface\n.\ndataElement\nor\nPersis-\ntencyKeyValueStorage\n.\nkeyValuePair\nin an updated\nmanifest\n, and the update\nstrategy is\ndelete\n, the\nPersistency\nshall remove that\nkey-value pair\nfrom the\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00013)\nUpdated\nkey-value pairs\nwith the update strategy\nkeepExisting\nwill not be\ntouched during an update.\nPersistency\nwill neither check the\nvalue\nnor the type of\nthe existing entry.\nTo support the conversion from one\nCppImplementationDataType\nto another (or\nto a different version of the same type) in the function registered using\nara::per::\nRegisterApplicationDataUpdateCallback\n,\nPersistency\nprovides the ability\nto read data types from a\nstorage\nthat are no longer used by the\napplication\n.\nThese types are configured in the\nmanifest\nas\npreviousDataType\nof a\nPersis-\ntencyKeyValueDataTypeMapping\nthat references a currently used type as\ncur-\nrentDataType\n.\nThere are two scenarios in which such a conversion is necessary:\n1. An existing data type has been modified for the new\napplication\n. The data\ntype still uses the same identifier.\n2. A new data type was introduced that replaces a data type that is no longer used\nin the new\napplication\n. The name of the old data type shall be formed as follows:\n59 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P61_140",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00446",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 61,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.6.3 Finalization of Persistent Data after Successful Update\nAfter installation and update,\nPersistency\nwill usually be called with\nara::per::\nUpdatePersistency\nwithin the verification phase of the\napplication\n. When this\nsucceeded, the\napplication\nwill be finalized by\nUpdate and Configuration\nManagement\nand then started again in normal execution mode. In this case,\nPer-\nsistency\nmay remove any backups that were created during a preceding update.\nBecause\nPersistency\nhas different update strategies (all\nstorages\nwith\nara::\nper::UpdatePersistency\nor single\nstorages\nwith\nara::per::OpenKeyVal-\nueStorage\nand\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\n), it is also up to the\napplication\nto decide when the backup data shall be removed, by calling\nara::per::CleanUp-\nPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00446]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::CleanUpPersistency\nis called by the\nap-\nplication\n, the\nPersistency\nshall remove all backup data of the\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00016)\nUpdate of\npersistent data\nis described in subsubsection 7.2.6.2.\n7.2.6.4 Roll-Back of Persistent Data after Failed Update\n[SWS_PER_00396]\nd\nWhen a\nstorage\nis opened by the\napplication\n, the\nPer-\nsistency\nshall compare the\ndeployment version\n(\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nversion\n) in the\nmanifest\nagainst the stored\ndeployment version\n. If the\nde-\nployment version\nin the\nmanifest\nis lower than the stored\ndeployment ver-\nsion\n, the\nPersistency\nshall compare the\ndeployment version\nin the\nmanifest\nagainst the\ndeployment version\nstored in backup data. If the\ndeployment ver-\nsions\nmatch, the\nPersistency\nshall restore the backup. Otherwise, it shall remove\nall\nstorages\n, and re-install the\npersistent data\nfrom the\nmanifest\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00014)\nInitialization of\npersistent data\nis described in subsubsection 7.2.6.1.\n7.2.6.5 Removal of Persistent Data\nPersistency\nis not able to remove its own data when the\nUpdate and Config-\nuration Management\nremoves an\napplication\n, because the\napplication\nwill\nnot be executed in this case, and therefore\nPersistency\ndoes not run. On the other\nhand, the\nUpdate and Configuration Management\nmay use the information in\nthe\nmanifest\n(\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersistencyCentralStorageURI\nand\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\ndeploymentUri\n) to obtain the locations of\nper-\nsistent data\n, and, if it has access to the locations, remove it.\n61 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P62_141",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00321",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 62,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.2.7 Resource Management Concepts\nThe\nPersistency\nsupports configuration of both an upper and a lower limit for the\nresources used by a\nKey-Value Storage\nor a\nFile Storage\n.\nThe lower limit may already be defined by the application developer using\nPersisten-\ncyInterface\n.\nminimumSustainedSize\n. During deployment, the integrator may up-\ndate the lower limit using\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nminimumSustainedSize\nand\nadd an upper limit using\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\n.\nThe\nPersistency\nwill actively monitor the upper limit, while the lower limit is ex-\npected to be checked during installation of the\nSoftwarePackage\nthat contains the\nExecutable\nwhich uses\nPersistency\n.\n[SWS_PER_00321]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall ensure that the space actually allocated\nby a\nstorage\nnever surpasses the amount configured by\nPersistencyDeploy-\nment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00010, RS_PER_00011)\nThis could be ensured by supervising all write accesses to\npersistent data\n. But\nthe implementation of the\nPersistency\nis free to chose other appropriate measures.\nThe\napplication\ncan also poll the amount of storage space currently occupied by a\ncomplete\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nby using\nara::per::GetCur-\nrentKeyValueStorageSize\nor\nara::per::GetCurrentFileStorageSize\n, re-\nspectively. Naturally, the returned values will not drop below a configured minimum\nsize (\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nminimumSustainedSize\n) or rise above a config-\nured maximum size (\nPersistencyDeployment\n.\nmaximumAllowedSize\n).\n[SWS_PER_00491]\nd\nara::per::GetCurrentKeyValueStorageSize\nshall re-\nturn the total size of the storage space currently allocated to a\nKey-Value Storage\n,\nincluding administrative data (apart from data stored in\nProcessToMachineMap-\nping\n.\npersistencyCentralStorageURI\n), redundant data, and backup data. The\nreported size may be inaccurate if the\nKey-Value Storage\nis currently open, or if an-\nother operation is currently being executed on the same\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00011)\nThe inaccuracy is mainly due to the fact that\nmetadata\nof the\nstorage\nis only up-\ndated when the\nstorage\nis fully synchronized, and predicting the\nmetadata\nsize is\nsometimes very difficult.\n[SWS_PER_00492]\nd\nara::per::GetCurrentFileStorageSize\nshall return the\ntotal size of the storage space currently allocated to a\nFile Storage\n, including ad-\nministrative data (apart from data stored in\nProcessToMachineMapping\n.\npersis-\ntencyCentralStorageURI\n), all its\nfiles\n, redundant data, and backup data. The\nreported size may be inaccurate if the\nFile Storage\nis currently open, or if another\noperation is currently being executed on the same\nstorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00011)\n62 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P63_142",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00506",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 63,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.3 Key-Value Storage specific Features\nTo access a\nKey-Value Storage\n, the\napplication\nhas to call\nara::per::\nOpenKeyValueStorage\nwith the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nderived from\nthe\nmanifest\n(a\nshortName\npath from the\nExecutable\nto a\nPortPrototype\nor\na mapping derived from\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithFunctionalClus-\nterMapping\n). This call will return an\nara::per::SharedHandle\nof an\nara::\nper::KeyValueStorage\n. The\nKey-Value Storage\nis closed when the\nara::\nper::SharedHandle\nand all of its copies go out of scope, or when\nara::core::\nDeinitialize\nis called.\n[SWS_PER_00506]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nis called, and\nPersistency\nis properly initialized as described in [SWS_PER_00408],\nPersis-\ntency\nshall create a temporary storage that provides access to the\nKey-Value\nStorage\nidentified by the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\n, and shall create\nand return an\nara::per::SharedHandle\nof an\nara::per::KeyValueStorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002)\nIf\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nis called without proper initialization,\n[SWS_PER_00410] applies.\nAll operations on a\nKey-Value Storage\nwill be done in a temporary storage cre-\nated during the call to\nara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\n, which the\napplica-\ntion\ncan persist using\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\n, or re-\nset to the last stored state with\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::DiscardPend-\ningChanges\n.\nTherefore, if the\nKey-Value Storage\nis just destructed (also implicitly when the\nProcess\nterminates), the\nKey-Value Storage\nis not updated, and the next time the\nKey-Value Storage\nis accessed, the\napplication\nwill see the last saved state.\n[SWS_PER_00331]\nd\nModifications of a\nKey-Value Storage\nthat have not been per-\nsisted with a call to\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nshall be dis-\ncarded when the\nKey-Value Storage\nis closed or the system is restarted, just as\nif\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::DiscardPendingChanges\nhad been called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\nChanges done by any thread (using a copy of the\nara::per::SharedHandle\n) will\nbe immediately visible in all other threads. This also applies to\nara::per::KeyVal-\nueStorage::DiscardPendingChanges\n, which resets the\nkey-value pairs\nin\nall threads, and to\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\n, which per-\nsists all changes done by any thread.\n[SWS_PER_00494]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall store all changes permanently that have been done to\nthe\nKey-Value Storage\nsince the last call to this method or since the\nKey-Value\nStorage\nwas opened.\nPersistency\nshall also update any configured\nredundancy\nwithin this call.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\n63 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P64_143",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00495",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 64,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nPlease note that depending on the implementation of\nPersistency\n, the configuration\nof an optionally used file system, and the capabilities of the used physical storage\ndevice, the actual storage of\nkey-value pairs\nmay be delayed. So, in case of an\nimmediate power down directly after this call, the physical data may be updated only\npartially or not at all. Therefore, data may be lost or, without\nredundancy\n, data may\neven be corrupted in this case.\nThe handling of\nredundancy\nis described in detail in subsection 7.2.5.\n[SWS_PER_00495]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::DiscardPend-\ningChanges\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall reset the\nKey-Value Storage\nto\nthe last persisted state, which is the state after the last call to\nara::per::Key-\nValueStorage::SyncToStorage\nor after opening the\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nSingle\nkey-value pairs\nof the\nKey-Value Storage\nare accessed using\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nand\nara::per::KeyValueStor-\nage::SetValue\n.\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nmay also be used\nto create a\nkey-value pair\n.\n[SWS_PER_00496]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present in the tem-\nporary storage, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002,\nRS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00497]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall check whether the tem-\nplated data type matches the stored data type, and otherwise return directly with\nkDataTypeMismatch\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00498]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\nwith the correct templated data type,\nPersistency\nshall return the stored\nvalue\nof the\nkey-value pair\n, or, if the\nvalue\nwas recently\nchanged by\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\n(also in another thread),\nthis new temporary\nvalue\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00002, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00499]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall check whether the tem-\nplated data type matches the stored data type, and otherwise return directly with\nkDataTypeMismatch\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00534]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\nwith the correct templated data type,\nPersistency\nshall store the new\nvalue\nof the\nkey-value pair\nin the temporary storage.\nc\n(RS_-\nPER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00501]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nis called,\nand the\nkey-value pair\ndoes not exist in the temporary storage,\nPersistency\nshall create the\nkey-value pair\nwith the templated data type and the provided\nvalue\nin the temporary storage.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n64 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P65_144",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00502",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 65,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nTo remove a single\nkey-value pair\n, the\napplication\nmay use\nara::\nper::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\n, while\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::\nRemoveAllKeys\nempties the\nKey-Value Storage\n. The type of a\nkey-value\npair\nmay be changed by first removing it, and then creating it with the new type.\n[SWS_PER_00502]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present\nin the temporary storage, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00535]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveKey\nis called\nfor an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall remove the\nkey-value pair\nfrom the temporary storage.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00503]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::RemoveAllKeys\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall remove all\nkey-value pairs\nfrom the temporary stor-\nage, resulting in an empty\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nFinally, the\napplication\ncan check for the existence of a single\nkey\nwith\nara::\nper::KeyValueStorage::KeyExists\n, check the current size of a\nvalue\nusing\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetCurrentValueSize\n, and acquire a list of all\ncurrently available\nkeys\nusing\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetAllKeys\n.\n[SWS_PER_00504]\nd\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::KeyExists\nshall return\ntrue if the\nkey\nis present in the temporary storage, otherwise it shall return false.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00565]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetCurrentVal-\nueSize\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nkey-value pair\nis present in the temporary\nstorage\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkKeyNot-\nFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00566]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetCurrentVal-\nueSize\nis called for an existing\nkey-value pair\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the\ncurrent size of its\nvalue\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n[SWS_PER_00505]\nd\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetAllKeys\nshall return\nan\nara::core::Vector\nof\nara::core::String\n, containing all the\nkeys\nthat are\npresent in the temporary storage. If the temporary storage is empty, an empty\nara::\ncore::Vector\nshall be returned.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003)\n7.3.1 Supported Data Types in Key-Value Storages\nThe\nPersistency\nsupports the following classes of data types in the functions\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\n(templated via\nT\n),\nara::per::Key-\nValueStorage::GetValue\nwith\nout\nparameter (templated via\nT\n), and\nara::per::\nKeyValueStorage::SetValue\n(templated via\nT\n) of a\nKey-Value Storage\n.\n65 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P66_145",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00302",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 66,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00302]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall be able to store all data types described\nin [10] in a\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\n[SWS_PER_00303]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall be able to store serialized binary data\nin a\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nPersistency\nshall accept serialized binary data in the\nform of an\nara::core::Vector\nof\nara::core::Byte\nor an\nara::core::Span\nof\nara::core::Byte\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001)\nThis allows the\napplication\nto store custom data types.\nPlease note that an\nara::core::Span\nof\nara::core::Byte\ncannot be returned\nby\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::GetValue\n. It can only be passed in to\nara::per::KeyValueStorage::SetValue\nand\nara::per::KeyValueStor-\nage::GetValue\nwith\nout\nparameter.\n[SWS_PER_00304]\nd\nThe\nPersistency\nshall be able to store all\nCppImple-\nmentationDataType\ns referenced by\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInter-\nface\n.\ndataTypeForSerialization\nor as\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageIn-\nterface\n.\ndataElement\nin the application design of a\nPersistencyKeyVal-\nueStorage\nin the corresponding\nKey-Value Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_-\nPER_00010)\nThe definitions of these data types are generated as described in [11]. Typically,\nPersistency\nwill generate serializers and deserializers for these types.\n66 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P67_146",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00507",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 67,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n7.4 File Storage specific Features\nTo access a\nFile Storage\n, the\napplication\nhas to call\nara::per::Open-\nFileStorage\nwith the\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier\nderived from the\nman-\nifest\n(a\nshortName\npath from the\nExecutable\nto a\nPortPrototype\nor a\nmapping derived from\nFunctionalClusterInteractsWithFunctionalClus-\nterMapping\n). This call will return an\nara::per::SharedHandle\nof an\nara::\nper::FileStorage\n. The\nFile Storage\nis closed when the\nara::per::\nSharedHandle\nand all of its copies go out of scope, or when\nara::core::Deini-\ntialize\nis called.\n[SWS_PER_00507]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\nis called, and\nPersis-\ntency\nis properly initialized as described in [SWS_PER_00408],\nPersistency\nshall\ncreate the necessary structures to access the\nFile Storage\nidentified by the\nara::\ncore::InstanceSpecifier\n, and create and return an\nara::per::SharedHan-\ndle\nof an\nara::per::FileStorage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nIf\nara::per::OpenFileStorage\nis called without proper initialization,\n[SWS_PER_00410] applies.\nTo check for the existence of a single\nfile\n, the\napplication\nmay call\nara::\nper::FileStorage::FileExists\n, and\nara::per::FileStorage::GetAll-\nFileNames\nwill return a list of all currently available\nfiles\nof the\nFile Storage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00508]\nd\nara::per::FileStorage::FileExists\nshall return true if\nthe\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n, otherwise it shall return false.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00004)\n[SWS_PER_00509]\nd\nara::per::FileStorage::GetAllFileNames\nshall return\nan\nara::core::Vector\nof\nara::core::String\n, containing the\nfile names\nof\nall the\nfiles\nthat are present in the\nFile Storage\n. If the\nFile Storage\nis empty,\nan empty\nara::core::Vector\nshall be returned.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nFiles\nmay be have been installed with the\napplication\nor may have\nbeen created during an update. To create new\nfiles\n, the\napplica-\ntion\nmay use\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadWrite\nor\nara::per::\nFileStorage::OpenFileWriteOnly\n, and it can use\nara::per::FileStor-\nage::DeleteFile\nto remove any\nfile\n.\n[SWS_PER_00510]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::DeleteFile\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n,\nand otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00511]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::DeleteFile\nis called for\nan existing\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall remove the\nfile\nfrom the\nFile Storage\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nTo access a\nfile\nof a\nFile Storage\n, the\napplication\nhas to call\nara::per::\nFileStorage::OpenFileReadWrite\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFil-\neReadOnly\n, or\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileWriteOnly\nwith the\nfile\n67 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
