      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nname\nof the\nfile\n. These calls will return an\nara::per::UniqueHandle\nof an\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nor\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\n.\n[SWS_PER_00551]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\n(or\none of the overloaded versions\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nor\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer) is called,\nPersistency\nshall first\ncheck whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n, and otherwise return di-\nrectly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00552]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\n(or the overloaded version\nara::per::FileStorage::\nOpenFileReadOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer) is called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the provided mode consists only of either\nkAtTheBeginning\nor\nkAtTheEnd\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkInvali-\ndOpenMode\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00512]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\n(or\none of the overloaded versions\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nor\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer) is called for an existing\nfile\nand\nwith a valid\nara::per::OpenMode\n,\nPersistency\nshall create the necessary struc-\ntures to access the\nfile\nidentified by the\nfile name\n, and create and return an\nara::per::UniqueHandle\nof an\nara::per::ReadAccessor\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00553]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileRead-\nWrite\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nor\nara::per::FileStorage::Open-\nFileWriteOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\n(or one of the overloaded versions\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadWrite\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer or\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileWriteOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer) is called,\nPersistency\nshall first check\nwhether the provided mode contains either\nkAtTheBeginning\n, possibly combined\nwith\nkTruncate\nand\nkAppend\n, or\nkAtTheEnd\n, possibly combined with\nkAppend\n, or\nonly\nkTruncate\n. Otherwise, the call shall return directly with\nkInvalidOpenMode\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00513]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadWrite\nor\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileWriteOnly\n(or one of their over-\nloaded versions\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadWrite\nwith\nara::\nper::OpenMode\n,\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileReadWrite\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer,\nara::per::FileStorage::Open-\nFileWriteOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\n, or\nara::per::FileStorage::\nOpenFileWriteOnly\nwith\nara::per::OpenMode\nand separate buffer) are called\nwith a valid\nara::per::OpenMode\n,\nPersistency\nshall create the necessary\nstructures to access the\nfile\nidentified by the\nfile name\n, and create and re-\nturn an\nara::per::UniqueHandle\nof an\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n68 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P69_148",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00457",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 69,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nThe\nfile\nis closed when the\nara::per::UniqueHandle\ngoes out of scope, or when\nara::core::Deinitialize\nis called.\n[SWS_PER_00457]\nd\nWhen a\nfile\nis closed,\nPersistency\nshall ensure that all\nchanges to the\nfile\nare persisted. This does not need to be done immediately like\nwhen\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nis called, but may happen\nat a later time, latest when the\nfile\nis opened again, or\nara::core::Deinitial-\nize\nis called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nSome of the overloads of the\nfile\nopening functions receive an\nara::per::Open-\nMode\nas an argument. OpenModes can be combined using the operators | and |=.\n[SWS_PER_00514]\nd\nara::per::operator\n| and\nara::per::operator\n|=\ntake two\nara::per::OpenMode\narguments and return the combined\nara::per::\nOpenMode\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nAll\nfiles\nof\nPersistency\nare implicitly readable, even when opened as \"write only\",\nwhich is expressed by\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\ninheriting from\nara::\nper::ReadAccessor\n. The\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nclass consequently also\noffers the methods related to\nfile\npositions.\n[SWS_PER_00515]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::SetPosition\nshall set the\nfile\nposition to the provided position. If the provided position is located outside of\nthe current content of the\nfile\n(including the position at the end of the\nfile\n),\nara::\nper::ReadAccessor::SetPosition\nshall keep the previous\nfile\nposition and re-\nturn\nkInvalidPosition\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00516]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::MovePosition\nshall move the\nfile\nposition to offset bytes according to the provided origin. If the new position would\nbe located outside of the current content of the\nfile\n(including the position at the end\nof the\nfile\n),\nara::per::ReadAccessor::MovePosition\nshall keep the previous\nfile\nposition and return\nkInvalidPosition\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00517]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetPosition\nshall return the\ncurrent read/write position in the\nfile\n. In the case of an empty\nfile\n, the position\nshall be returned as\n0\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00518]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::IsEof\nshall return true if the\nposition is the last possible position in the\nfile\n, otherwise false.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nara::per::ReadAccessor::IsEof\nwill return true if the current position corre-\nsponds to the total\nfile\nsize, which can be obtained separately using\nara::per::\nReadAccessor::GetSize\n. In other words, true is only returned when the current\nposition is at the position directly after the last character in the\nfile\n, or if the\nfile\nis\nempty.\n[SWS_PER_00519]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetSize\nshall return the cur-\nrent total size of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nPersistency\ndoes not care whether the content of a\nfile\nis text or some binary\ndata, and therefore offers separate methods to access the\nfile\ncontent as text or as\n69 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P70_149",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00520",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 70,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nbinary data. To read content from a text\nfile\n, the\napplication\nmay use one of the\nfollowing methods of the\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nclass:\n[SWS_PER_00520]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::PeekChar\nshall return the\ncharacter at the current\nfile\nposition without changing the position.\nc\n(RS_PER_-\n00004)\n[SWS_PER_00521]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetChar\nshall return the char-\nacter at the current\nfile\nposition and advance the position by one.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00522]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadText\nshall read the text\nfrom the current position to the end of the\nfile\nand return it as an\nara::core::\nString\n. The position shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00523]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadText\nshall read the\nn\ncharacters of text from the current position and return them as an\nara::core::\nString\n. The position shall be incremented by\nn\n. In case the end of the\nfile\nis\nreached during this operation, the available characters shall be returned, and the posi-\ntion shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00524]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadLine\nshall read all char-\nacters until the delimiter (defaulting to the newline character) or the end of the\nfile\nis reached, and return them as a\nara::core::String\n. The delimiter shall not be\nincluded in the returned\nara::core::String\n. The position shall be set to the char-\nacter following the delimiter or the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004, RS_AP_00136)\nAll these methods return characters with a size of eight bits, which are just so-called\ncode units\nin case of\nUTF-8\n, not\ncode points\n. Therefore, these methods might\nreturn incomplete\ncode points\n.\nPersistency\nitself does not change or interpret\nthe content of a\nfile\nwhen accessing it in text mode. It is assumed, though, that\nfiles\nin the\nFile Storage\nare encoded as\nUTF-8\n(see [RS_AP_00136]). It is also\nassumed that line endings are handled according to\nUNIX\nconventions, i.e. just\nLF\n(\"\n\\n\n\").\n[SWS_PER_CONSTR_00006]\nd\nIf a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith\ncategory\nequal to\nSTRING\nis used as\nPersistencyDataElement\n, then the encoding of this\nstring\ndata type is expected to be\nUTF-8\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00003, RS_PER_00004, RS_-\nAP_00136)\nThis means that a\nCppImplementationDataType\ncan only be mapped to an\nApplicationDataType\nof\ncategory STRING\nwhere attribute\nswDataDefProps\n.\nswTextProps\n.\nbaseType\n.\nbaseTypeDefinition\n.\nbaseTypeEncoding\nis set to the\nvalue\nUTF-8\nas defined by [constr_5035]. If a\nCppImplementationDataType\nwith-\nout an\nApplicationDataType\nis used there is no formal description about the\nUTF-\n8\nencoding in the\nServiceInterface\ndescription.\nThe following methods of the\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nclass can be used by an\napplication\nto read binary content from a file:\n[SWS_PER_00525]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::PeekByte\nshall return the byte\nat the current\nfile\nposition without changing the position.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n70 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P71_150",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00526",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 71,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n[SWS_PER_00526]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::GetByte\nshall return the byte\nat the current\nfile\nposition and advance the position by one.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00527]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadBinary\nshall read binary\ndata from the current position to the end of the\nfile\nand return it as an\nara::core::\nVector\nof\nara::core::Byte\n. The position shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00528]\nd\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadBinary\nshall read the\nn\ncharacters of text from the current position and return them as an\nara::core::Vec-\ntor\nof\nara::core::Byte\n. The position shall be incremented by\nn\n. In case the end\nof the\nfile\nis reached during this operation, the available bytes shall be returned, and\nthe position shall be set to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nTo write text to\nfiles\n, the\napplication\nmay use the\nara::per::ReadWriteAc-\ncessor::WriteText\nmethod or the\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::opera-\ntor\n<< of the\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\nclass, which treat text in the same\nway as described above for e.g.\nara::per::ReadAccessor::ReadText\n.\n[SWS_PER_00557]\nd\nIf the\nfile\nwas opened with\nara::per::OpenMode\nset to\nkAppend\n,\nPersistency\nshall always set the current position to the end of the\nfile\nbefore writing data to the\nfile\naccording to [SWS_PER_00529], [SWS_PER_00530],\nor [SWS_PER_00531].\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00529]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::WriteText\nshall write\nthe characters provided as\nara::core::StringView\nto the\nfile\nat the current\nposition, possibly overwriting current content and advancing the end of the\nfile\nif\nnecessary. The position shall be set to the character following the last character that\nwas written during this operation, or to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00530]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::operator\n<< shall write\nthe characters provided as\nara::core::StringView\nto the\nfile\nat the current po-\nsition, possibly overwriting current content and advancing the end of the\nfile\nif nec-\nessary. The position shall be set to the character following the last character that was\nwritten during this operation, or to the end of the\nfile\n. If an error occurs during this\noperation, the\nfile\ncontent might be partially updated and the resulting\nfile\nposition\nmight not be as expected.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nTo write binary data to a\nfile\n, the\napplication\nmay use the method\nara::per::\nReadWriteAccessor::WriteBinary\nof the\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\nclass. See also [SWS_PER_00557] for\nara::per::OpenMode kAppend\n.\n[SWS_PER_00531]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::WriteBinary\nshall\nwrite the bytes provided as\nara::core::Span\nof\nara::core::Byte\nto the\nfile\nat\nthe current position, possibly overwriting current content and advancing the end of the\nfile\nif necessary. The position shall be set to the byte following the last byte that was\nwritten during this operation, or to the end of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nThe\napplication\nmay use\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SetFileSize\nto\nexplicitly set the\nfile\nsize to a defined value in order to truncate a\nfile\nor to empty\n71 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P72_151",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00532",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 72,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nit. Enlarging\nfiles\nis not supported by\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::Set-\nFileSize\n.\n[SWS_PER_00532]\nd\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SetFileSize\nshall set\nthe\nfile\nsize to the provided value. The read/write position shall be set to the end of\nthe\nfile\nif the current position is higher than the new\nfile\nsize. If the provided value\nis larger than the current\nfile\nsize,\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SetFile-\nSize\nshall return\nkInvalidSize\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nWhen the\napplication\nchanged a\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nwill ensure that these\nchanges are persisted. This can happen at any time, and latest when the\nfile\nis closed. To trigger an additional synchronization of the\nfile\ncontent to the per-\nsistent storage, the\napplication\nmay call\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::\nSyncToFile\n.\n[SWS_PER_00533]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall store the content of the\nfile\n.\nPersistency\nshall also\nupdate any configured\nredundancy\nwithin this call.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nPlease note that depending on the implementation of\nPersistency\n, the configuration\nof an optionally used file system, and the capabilities of the used physical storage\ndevice, the actual storage of the\nfile\ncontent may be delayed. So, in case of an\nimmediate power down directly after this call, the physical data may be updated only\npartially or not at all. Therefore, data may be lost or, without\nredundancy\n, data may\neven be corrupted in this case.\nThe handling of\nredundancy\nis described in detail in subsection 7.2.5.\n7.4.1 Access to Additional Information about Files\nTo gain information about stored\nfiles\n, the\nPersistency\nprovides the\nmethods\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nand\nara::per::\nFileStorage::GetFileInfo\n.\nThe\napplication\ncan poll the amount of storage space currently occupied by a single\nfile\nusing\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nof an open\nFile\nStorage\n.\n[SWS_PER_00549]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nis\ncalled,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Stor-\nage\n, and otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00493]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\nis\ncalled for an existing\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the current size of the passed\nfile\n. This size shall reflect only the data contained in the\nfile\n. In case the\nfile\nis\ncurrently open,\nPersistency\nshall return the current size of the\nfile\n, which might\ndiffer from the size of the\nfile\nin the\nstorage\nif the last changes are not yet synchro-\nnized. Otherwise, if the\nfile\nis not open,\nPersistency\nshall return the size of any\n72 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P73_152",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00492",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 73,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\nexisting instance of the\nfile\nwithout checking the consistency/validity of the\nfile\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00011)\nPlease note that administrative and redundant information is not included in the\nfile\nsize reported by\nara::per::FileStorage::GetCurrentFileSize\n, while it is in-\ncluded in the total size of the\nFile Storage\nreturned by\nara::per::GetCurrent-\nFileStorageSize\n(see [SWS_PER_00492]).\nUsing\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\n, the\napplication\ncan acquire\ninformation about the time the\nfile\nwas created (\ncreationTime\n), last modified (\nmodificationTime\n), and last accessed (\naccessTime\n), and how and by whom it\nwas created (\nfileCreationState\n) and last modified (\nfileModificationState\n).\n[SWS_PER_00550]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\nis called,\nPersistency\nshall first check whether the\nfile\nis present in the\nFile Storage\n,\nand otherwise return directly with\nkFileNotFound\n.\nc\n(RS_AP_00128)\n[SWS_PER_00440]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\nis called for\nan existing but currently not opened\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall gather the required\ninformation from any existing instance of the\nfile\n(without checking the consistency/-\nvalidity of this\nfile\n) into a\nara::per::FileInfo\nstruct and return it to the\nappli-\ncation\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\n[SWS_PER_00570]\nd\nWhen\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\nis called for\nan existing and currently opened\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the time when the\nfile\nwas opened for\naccessTime\nand\ncreationTime\n(the latter only if the\nfile\nwas also created at the same time).\nFor the\nmodificationTime\n, before the\napplication\nwrote anything to the\nfile\n,\nPersistency\nshall return the original modification time. Afterwards,\nPersistency\nshall return the time the\nfile\nwas last modified by the\napplication\nor\nara::per::\nReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile\nwas last called.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nIn case the\nPersistency\nuses a file system of the underlying OS, part of that infor-\nmation (like the creation or access time) can be obtained from the file system. Please\nnote that the time stamps returned by\nara::per::FileStorage::GetFileInfo\non a closed\nfile\nmight be later than the ones returned by\nPersistency\nwhile the\nfile\nwas still opened, because\nPersistency\nhas no control over the actual point in\ntime at which a file system (if used) updates these time stamps.\n[SWS_PER_00458]\nd\nIf\ncreationTime\n,\nmodificationTime\n, or\naccessTime\nare\nnot available, they shall be set to\n0\n.\nc\n(RS_PER_00004)\nAs an example, the\naccessTime\nis not available for a read-only\nFile Storage\n, and\nwould therefore be reported as midnight 1970-01-01.\n73 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P74_153",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 74,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8 API Specification\nThe APIs for accessing\nFile Storages\nand\nKey-Value Storage\nare completely\nseparate, and therefore divided into separate sections. Additional sections describe\ncommon functionality.\nThe API of\nPersistency\nis designed around the\nara::per::SharedHandle\nand\nara::per::UniqueHandle\n, which are returned by factory functions like\nara::\nper::OpenKeyValueStorage\nor\nara::per::FileStorage::OpenFileRead-\nWrite\n. The classes defined in this chapter cannot be constructed directly by the\nAdaptive Application\n, and consequently the default constructors are considered\nto be not publicly accessible (i.e. to be deleted, private, or protected).\n8.1 General Features of Persistency\n8.1.1 ara::core Types\nThe\nara::per\nAPI is based heavily on the\nara::core\ntypes defined in [2].\nara::core::Result\nis used wherever possible, and because of this, most methods\nare defined as\nnoexcept\n.\nConsequently, in situations where memory cannot be allocated for new objects, the\nPersistency\nshall terminate the process by calling\nara::core::Abort\n(see [2]).\n74 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P75_154",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00356",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 75,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.1.2 Installation and Update of Persistent Data\nThe\nPersistency\ninstalls/updates its\nKey-Value Storages\nand\nFile Storages\neither during the validation of a freshly installed/updated\napplication\nin the\nara::\nper::UpdatePersistency\ncall, or when the\nstorages\nare opened for the first\ntime. It allows to monitor these operations with a callback function installed with\nara::per::RegisterApplicationDataUpdateCallback\n. The\napplication\nmay also restore the\nPersistency\nto the initial state (i.e. the state that it would have\nif it was installed with the current\nmanifest\n) with a call to\nara::per::ResetPer-\nsistency\n.\n8.1.2.1 RegisterApplicationDataUpdateCallback\n[SWS_PER_00356] Definition of API function ara::per::RegisterApplicationData\nUpdateCallback\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P75_155",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00356",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 75,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The callback function to be called by Persistency after an update of\npersistent data took place. The function will be called with the short\nName path of an updated Key-Value Storage or File Storage, and\nwith the contract version with which the Persistency was last\naccessed."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P75_156",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00356",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 75,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Registers an application data update callback with Persistency.\nThe provided callback function will be called by Persistency if an update of stored application\ndata might be necessary. This decision is based on the contract versions.\nThe contract version that last accessed Persistency is provided as an argument to the callback,\nas well as the InstanceSpecifier referring to the updated Key-Value Storage or File Storage.\nBased on this information, the application can decide which updates are actually necessary, e.g.\na migration from any older contract version could be supported, with different steps required for\neach of these.\nThe provided function will be called from the context of UpdatePersistency(), OpenKeyValue\nStorage(), or OpenFileStorage()."
    },

      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P75_157",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00356",

    },

    },

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P78_173",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 78,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00009, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_00120, RS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128,\nRS_AP_00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00139)\n78 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P79_174",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00432",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 79,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.1.3 Redundancy Handling\nThe\nPersistency\nsupports redundant storage of\nKey-Value Storages\n,\nFile\nStorages\n, and the\nkey-value pairs\nand\nfiles\ncontained in these. An error in\nthe stored data that can be fixed using the redundantly stored data will be implicitly\nfixed when the\nKey-Value Storage\nor\nFile Storage\nis accessed, an error is only\nreturned by\nPersistency\nwhen the redundancy fails. To be able to track whether\nstorage\nerrors have been fixed using the available redundancy, the\napplication\ncan register the following callback function.\n8.1.3.1 RecoveryReportKind\n[SWS_PER_00432] Definition of API enum ara::per::RecoveryReportKind\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P79_175",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00432",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 79,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n79 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P80_176",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00433",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P80_177",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00433",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00008, RS_AP_00122, RS_AP_00125, RS_AP_00143)\n8.1.3.2 RegisterRecoveryReportCallback\n[SWS_PER_00433] Definition of API function ara::per::RegisterRecoveryReport\nCallback\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P80_178",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00433",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "RegisterRecoveryReportCallback(std::function< void(const ara::core::InstanceSpecifier\n&storage, ara::per::RecoveryReportKind recoveryReportKind, ara::core::Vector<\nara::core::String > reportedElements, ara::core::Vector< std::uint8_t > reportedInstances)>\nrecoveryReportCallback)"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P80_179",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00433",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "void RegisterRecoveryReportCallback (std::function< void(const\nara::core::InstanceSpecifier &storage, ara::per::RecoveryReportKind\nrecoveryReportKind, ara::core::Vector< ara::core::String > reported\nElements, ara::core::Vector< std::uint8_t > reportedInstances)>\nrecoveryReportCallback) noexcept;"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P80_180",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00433",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The callback function to be called by Persistency to report errors in\nthe stored data that were corrected using the available redundancy.\nThe function will be called with the shortName path of the affected\nKey-Value Storage or File Storage in storage and information on\nwhat has been corrected, placed in the parameters recoveryReport\nKind, reportedElements, and reportedInstances."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P80_181",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00433",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 80,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n80 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P81_182",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 81,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P81_183",
      "source_element": null,
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 81,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Register a recovery reporting callback with Persistency.\nThis callback can be used in safety-aware applications to detect actions of the Persistency that\nare related to the correctness of the persisted data and the reliability of the storage."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P81_184",

      "source_page": 82,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.1.4 Handle Classes\nThis section contains the definition of the handle classes used in the API of the\nPer-\nsistency\n. The\nara::per::SharedHandle\n(templated via\ntypenameT\n) is used to\nprovide shared access to either a\nara::per::KeyValueStorage\nor a\nara::per::\nFileStorage\n, while the\nara::per::UniqueHandle\n(templated via\ntypenameT\n)\nis used to provide non-shared access to either a\nara::per::ReadAccessor\nor a\nara::per::ReadWriteAccessor\nto a\nFile Storage\n.\n8.1.4.1 SharedHandle Class\n[SWS_PER_00362] Definition of API class ara::per::SharedHandle\nd"

    {

      "source_page": 97,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_AP_00120, RS_AP_00121)\n97 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_245",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.2 Key-Value Storage\nThis section lists all functions and classes that are required to operate a\nKey-Value\nStorage\n.\nThe following functions are used to get access to a\nKey-Value Storage\n, to recover\nas much as possible after it was corrupted, to reset it to the deployed defaults, and to\nget the amount of storage space allocated to the\nKey-Value Storage\n.\n8.2.1 OpenKeyValueStorage\n[SWS_PER_00052] Definition of API function ara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_246",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyKey\nValueStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_247",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface configured for this\nExecutable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_248",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if RecoverKeyValue\nStorage or ResetKeyValueStorage is currently being executed for\nthe same Key-Value Storage."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P98_249",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00052",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 98,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n98 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_250",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_251",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Opens a Key-Value Storage.\nOpenKeyValueStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently\nbeing modified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset\nPersistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage.\nBecause multiple threads can access the same Key-Value Storage concurrently, the Key-Value\nStorage might not be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of\nscope. It will only be closed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same Key-Value Storage\nwent out of scope."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_252",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00003, RS_PER_00010, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_00120, RS_AP_00121,\nRS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128, RS_AP_00129, RS_AP_00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_-\nAP_00137, RS_AP_00139, RS_AP_00144, RS_AP_00147)\n8.2.2 RecoverKeyValueStorage\n[SWS_PER_00333] Definition of API function ara::per::RecoverKeyValueStorage\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_253",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyKey\nValueStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_254",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface configured for this\nExecutable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_255",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if ResetKeyValue\nStorage is currently being executed for the same Key-Value\nStorage, or a SharedHandle of the same Key-Value Storage is\ncurrently in use."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P99_256",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00333",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 99,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n99 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_257",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_258",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Recovers a Key-ValueStorage.\nRecoverKeyValueStorage allows to recover a Key-Value Storage when the redundancy checks\nfail.\nIt will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently open, or when it is\nmodified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset\nPersistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage.\nThis method does a best-effort recovery of all key-value pairs. After recovery, keys might show\noutdated or initial value, or might be lost."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_259",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00003, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_-\n00120, RS_AP_00121, RS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128, RS_AP_00129, RS_AP_-\n00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00137, RS_AP_00139)\n8.2.3 ResetKeyValueStorage\n[SWS_PER_00334] Definition of API function ara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_260",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyKey\nValueStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_261",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface configured for this\nExecutable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_262",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if RecoverKeyValue\nStorage is currently being executed for the same Key-Value\nStorage, or a SharedHandle of the same Key-Value Storage is\ncurrently in use."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P100_263",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00334",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 100,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n100 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P101_264",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00405",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 101,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P101_265",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00405",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 101,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Resets a Key-Value Storage to the initial state.\nResetKeyValueStorage allows to reset a Key-Value Storage to the initial state, containing only\nkey-value pairs which were deployed from the manifest, with their initial values. Afterwards, the\nKey-Value Storage will appear as if it was newly installed from the current manifest.\nIt will fail with kResourceBusy when the Key-Value Storage is currently open, or when it is\nmodified by a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, Reset\nPersistency, RecoverKeyValueStorage, or ResetKeyValueStorage."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P101_266",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00405",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 101,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00003, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_-\n00120, RS_AP_00121, RS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128, RS_AP_00129, RS_AP_-\n00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00137, RS_AP_00139)\n8.2.4 GetCurrentKeyValueStorageSize\n[SWS_PER_00405] Definition of API function ara::per::GetCurrentKeyValueStor-\nageSize\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P101_267",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00405",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 101,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyKey\nValueStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P101_268",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00405",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",

      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00002, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_00120, RS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128,\nRS_AP_00129, RS_AP_00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00139)\n113 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_326",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n8.3 File Storage\nThis section lists all functions and classes that are required to operate a\nFile Stor-\nage\n.\nThe following functions are used to get access to a\nFile Storage\n, to recover as\nmuch as possible after it was corrupted, to reset it to the deployed defaults, and to get\nthe amount of storage space allocated to the\nFile Storage\n. In addition, operators\nare present to combine the\nara::per::OpenMode\nvalues passed as\nmode\nto the\nOpenFile\n*\nfunctions.\n8.3.1 OpenFileStorage\n[SWS_PER_00116] Definition of API function ara::per::OpenFileStorage\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_327",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyFile\nStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_328",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface configured for this Executable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_329",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if RecoverAllFiles or\nResetAllFiles is currently being executed for the same File Storage."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P114_330",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00116",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 114,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n114 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_331",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_332",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Opens a File Storage.\nOpenFileStorage will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently being modified\nby a call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency,\nRecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles.\nBecause multiple threads can access the same File Storage concurrently, the File Storage might\nnot be closed when the SharedHandle returned by this function goes out of scope. It will only be\nclosed when all SharedHandles that refer to the same File Storage went out of scope."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_333",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00004, RS_PER_00010, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_-\n00120, RS_AP_00121, RS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128, RS_AP_00129, RS_AP_-\n00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00137, RS_AP_00139, RS_AP_00144, RS_AP_-\n00147)\n8.3.2 RecoverAllFiles\n[SWS_PER_00335] Definition of API function ara::per::RecoverAllFiles\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_334",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyFile\nStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_335",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface configured for this Executable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_336",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if ResetAllFiles is\ncurrently being executed for the same File Storage, or a Shared\nHandle of the same File Storage is currently in use."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P115_337",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00335",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 115,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "5\n115 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_338",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Specification of Persistency\nAUTOSAR AP R23-11\n4"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_339",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Recovers a File Storage, including all files.\nRecoverAllFiles recovers a File Storage when the redundancy checks fail.\nIt will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently open, or when it is modified by\na call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency,\nRecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles.\nThis method does a best-effort recovery of all files. After recovery, files might show outdated or\ninitial content, or might be lost."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_340",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00004, RS_PER_00009, RS_PER_00010, RS_AP_-\n00119, RS_AP_00120, RS_AP_00121, RS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00128, RS_AP_-\n00129, RS_AP_00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00137, RS_AP_00139)\n8.3.3 ResetAllFiles\n[SWS_PER_00336] Definition of API function ara::per::ResetAllFiles\nd"
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_341",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "The shortName path of a PortPrototype typed by a PersistencyFile\nStorageInterface."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_342",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if the passed InstanceSpecifier does not match any\nPersistencyFileStorageInterface configured for this Executable."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_343",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Returned if UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, or Reset\nPersistency is currently being executed, or if RecoverAllFiles is\ncurrently being executed for the same File Storage, or a Shared\nHandle of the same File Storage is currently in use."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_344",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Resets a File Storage, including all files.\nResetAllFiles resets a File Storage to the initial state, containing only the files which were\ndeployed from the manifest, with their initial content. Afterwards, the File Storage will appear as\nif it was newly installed from the current manifest.\nIt will fail with kResourceBusy when the File Storage is currently open, or when it is modified by\na call from another thread to UpdatePersistency, CleanUpPersistency, ResetPersistency,\nRecoverAllFiles, or ResetAllFiles."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P116_345",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00336",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 116,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "116 of 196 Document ID 858: AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency"

      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00423",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",

    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P152_489",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00423",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 152,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Writes the content of a StringView to the file.\nThe time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo\nFile can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content.\nIn case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might\nnot have changed.\nThe expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows:\n\u000f\nkPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely\ndestroyed.\n\u000f\nkEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but\ncould not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file.\n\u000f\nkOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the\noperation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at\nthe end of the file."
    },
    {
      "id": "SNIP_per_AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_P_P152_490",
      "source_element": "SWS_PER_00423",
      "source_document": "AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency",
      "source_page": 152,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "c\n(RS_PER_00001, RS_PER_00004, RS_AP_00119, RS_AP_00120, RS_AP_00121,\nRS_AP_00127, RS_AP_00132, RS_AP_00135, RS_AP_00136, RS_AP_00139)\n8.3.14.5 ReadWriteAccessor::WriteBinary\n[SWS_PER_00423] Definition of API function ara::per::ReadWriteAcces-\nsor::WriteBinary\nd"

      "source_page": 153,
      "category": "architectural_role",
      "verbatim_text": "Writes the content of a Span of Byte to the file.\nThe time when the content is persisted depends on the implementation of Persistency. SyncTo\nFile can be used to force Persistency to persist the file content.\nIn case of an error, the file content might be corrupted, and the current position might or might\nnot have changed.\nThe expected state of the file for each supported error can be expected to be as follows:\n\u000f\nkPhysicalStorageFailure: The state of the file is unknown. It could have been entirely\ndestroyed.\n\u000f\nkEncryptionFailed: The content of the file and the current position will have been updated, but\ncould not be persisted. The persisted file will reflect an older version of the file.\n\u000f\nkOutOfStorageSpace: The content of the file will have been updated, but the part of the\noperation that exceeded the quota will have been discarded. The current position will be at\nthe end of the file."
    },

  "bisheriges_fragment": "<div class=\"ai module-guide\"><p class=\"ai-note\">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Zweck und Systemgrenze</h4><p><code>ara::per</code> macht konfigurierte persistente Daten für Adaptive Applications zugänglich. Das Modell unterscheidet Key-Value Storages als Mengen typisierter Schlüssel-Wert-Paare und File Storages als Mengen benannter Dateien; beide können pro Anwendung kombiniert werden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1\">SWS Persistency §7.1 „The Architecture of Persistency“</a></p><p>Die Storage-Instanz ist nicht frei wählbar, sondern wird durch einen <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> auf eine manifestierte Persistency-Schnittstelle bezogen. Zugriffsrechte können read-only, read/write, write-only oder – für Anwendungen – write-only-once sein. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1\">SWS Persistency §7.1.1 „Configuration of Persistency“</a></p><h4>Entscheidung: Schlüssel oder Datei</h4><p>Wähle <code>KeyValueStorage</code> für adressierbare, typisierte Zustände mit einer expliziten Synchronisierungsgrenze; wähle <code>FileStorage</code> für dateiförmige Inhalte und Accessor-basiertes Lesen bzw. Schreiben. Initialwerte und initiale Dateien können mit Installation oder Update mitgeliefert werden. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2\">SWS Persistency §7.1.2 „Configuration of Key-Value Storages“</a> <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3\">SWS Persistency §7.1.3 „Configuration of File Storages“</a></p><p class=\"interp\"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Die Auswahl ist ein Datenmodell-Entscheid: kleine, logisch getrennte Zustände profitieren von Schlüsseln; zusammenhängende oder streamartige Inhalte passen eher zur Datei-Schnittstelle. Sie folgt aus den unterschiedlichen, in der Spezifikation beschriebenen Zugriffsmodellen.</p><h4>Betriebsmodell und Datenhaltbarkeit</h4><p>Ein geöffneter Key-Value Storage arbeitet zunächst auf temporären Daten. <code>SyncToStorage</code> schreibt alle Änderungen seit Öffnen oder letzter Synchronisierung dauerhaft und aktualisiert konfigurierte Redundanz; ohne Synchronisierung werden Änderungen beim Schließen oder Neustart verworfen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3\">SWS Persistency §7.3 „Key-Value Storage specific Features“</a></p><p>Bei Dateien wird die konkrete Datei über einen Accessor geöffnet. Schreibzugriffe können über <code>SyncToFile</code> gezielt in den physischen Speicher übertragen werden; Ownership des Accessors ist exklusiv. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4\">SWS Persistency §7.4 „File Storage specific Features“</a></p><h4>Schutz, Wiederherstellung und Ressourcen</h4><p>Redundanz kann Integrität über Prüfsummen oder mehrere Kopien absichern; bei nicht behebbaren Befunden kann ein Recovery-Report-Callback die Anwendung informieren. Eine Wiederherstellung kann initiale oder ältere Daten ergeben und ist daher fachlich zu prüfen. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.4\">SWS Persistency §7.2.4 „Redundancy Concepts“</a></p><p>Der konfigurierte Höchstwert begrenzt tatsächlich belegten Speicher. Die Größenabfragen enthalten Metadaten sowie Redundanz- und Backupbedarf und können bei offenem Storage oder parallelen Operationen ungenau sein. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.6\">SWS Persistency §7.2.6 „Resource Management Concepts“</a></p><h4>Installation, Update und Rollback</h4><p>Die Target Configuration kann vordefinierte Werte und Dateien einbringen. Während der Verifikationsphase kann <code>UpdatePersistency</code> Änderungen nach neuen Konfigurationsdaten ausführen; nach erfolgreicher Finalisierung entfernt <code>CleanUpPersistency</code> Sicherungsdaten. Ist eine ältere Konfiguration aktiviert, erfolgt abhängig von der gespeicherten Backupversion eine Wiederherstellung oder Neuinstallation. <a class=\"docref\" href=\"https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.5\">SWS Persistency §7.2.5 „Installation and Update of Persistent Data“</a></p><div <div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Zweck und Systemgrenze</h4><p><code>ara::per</code> macht konfigurierte persistente Daten für Adaptive Applications zugänglich. Das Modell unterscheidet Key-Value Storages als Mengen typisierter Schlüssel-Wert-Paare und File Storages als Mengen benannter Dateien; beide können pro Anwendung kombiniert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS Persistency §7.1 „The Architecture of Persistency“</a></p><p>Die Storage-Instanz ist nicht frei wählbar, sondern wird durch einen <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> auf eine manifestierte Persistency-Schnittstelle bezogen. Zugriffsrechte können read-only, read/write, write-only oder – für Anwendungen – write-only-once sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1">SWS Persistency §7.1.1 „Configuration of Persistency“</a></p><h4>Entscheidung: Schlüssel oder Datei</h4><p>Wähle <code>KeyValueStorage</code> für adressierbare, typisierte Zustände mit einer expliziten Synchronisierungsgrenze; wähle <code>FileStorage</code> für dateiförmige Inhalte und Accessor-basiertes Lesen bzw. Schreiben. Initialwerte und initiale Dateien können mit Installation oder Update mitgeliefert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Persistency §7.1.2 „Configuration of Key-Value Storages“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3">SWS Persistency §7.1.3 „Configuration of File Storages“</a></p><p class="interp"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Die Auswahl ist ein Datenmodell-Entscheid: kleine, logisch getrennte Zustände profitieren von Schlüsseln; zusammenhängende oder streamartige Inhalte passen eher zur Datei-Schnittstelle. Sie folgt aus den unterschiedlichen, in der Spezifikation beschriebenen Zugriffsmodellen.</p><h4>Betriebsmodell und Datenhaltbarkeit</h4><p>Ein geöffneter Key-Value Storage arbeitet zunächst auf temporären Daten. <code>SyncToStorage</code> schreibt alle Änderungen seit Öffnen oder letzter Synchronisierung dauerhaft und aktualisiert konfigurierte Redundanz; ohne Synchronisierung werden Änderungen beim Schließen oder Neustart verworfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS Persistency §7.3 „Key-Value Storage specific Features“</a></p><p>Bei Dateien wird die konkrete Datei über einen Accessor geöffnet. Schreibzugriffe können über <code>SyncToFile</code> gezielt in den physischen Speicher übertragen werden; Ownership des Accessors ist exklusiv. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS Persistency §7.4 „File Storage specific Features“</a></p><h4>Schutz, Wiederherstellung und Ressourcen</h4><p>Redundanz kann Integrität über Prüfsummen oder mehrere Kopien absichern; bei nicht behebbaren Befunden kann ein Recovery-Report-Callback die Anwendung informieren. Eine Wiederherstellung kann initiale oder ältere Daten ergeben und ist daher fachlich zu prüfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.4">SWS Persistency §7.2.4 „Redundancy Concepts“</a></p><p>Der konfigurierte Höchstwert begrenzt tatsächlich belegten Speicher. Die Größenabfragen enthalten Metadaten sowie Redundanz- und Backupbedarf und können bei offenem Storage oder parallelen Operationen ungenau sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.6">SWS Persistency §7.2.6 „Resource Management Concepts“</a></p><h4>Installation, Update und Rollback</h4><p>Die Target Configuration kann vordefinierte Werte und Dateien einbringen. Während der Verifikationsphase kann <code>UpdatePersistency</code> Änderungen nach neuen Konfigurationsdaten ausführen; nach erfolgreicher Finalisierung entfernt <code>CleanUpPersistency</code> Sicherungsdaten. Ist eine ältere Konfiguration aktiviert, erfolgt abhängig von der gespeicherten Backupversion eine Wiederherstellung oder Neuinstallation. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.5">SWS Persistency §7.2.5 „Installation and Update of Persistent Data“</a></p><div <div class="ai module-guide"><p class="ai-note">Automatisch generierte Beschreibung, inhaltlich abgeleitet aus den referenzierten AUTOSAR-R25-11-Dokumenten (SWS-Spezifikation und begleitende Standarddokumente) — kein offizieller AUTOSAR-Text. Als Interpretation gekennzeichnete Aussagen sind Schlussfolgerungen aus den Quellen.</p><h4>Zweck und Systemgrenze</h4><p><code>ara::per</code> macht konfigurierte persistente Daten für Adaptive Applications zugänglich. Das Modell unterscheidet Key-Value Storages als Mengen typisierter Schlüssel-Wert-Paare und File Storages als Mengen benannter Dateien; beide können pro Anwendung kombiniert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.1">SWS Persistency §7.1 „The Architecture of Persistency“</a></p><p>Die Storage-Instanz ist nicht frei wählbar, sondern wird durch einen <code>ara::core::InstanceSpecifier</code> auf eine manifestierte Persistency-Schnittstelle bezogen. Zugriffsrechte können read-only, read/write, write-only oder – für Anwendungen – write-only-once sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.1">SWS Persistency §7.1.1 „Configuration of Persistency“</a></p><h4>Entscheidung: Schlüssel oder Datei</h4><p>Wähle <code>KeyValueStorage</code> für adressierbare, typisierte Zustände mit einer expliziten Synchronisierungsgrenze; wähle <code>FileStorage</code> für dateiförmige Inhalte und Accessor-basiertes Lesen bzw. Schreiben. Initialwerte und initiale Dateien können mit Installation oder Update mitgeliefert werden. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.2">SWS Persistency §7.1.2 „Configuration of Key-Value Storages“</a> <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.1.3">SWS Persistency §7.1.3 „Configuration of File Storages“</a></p><p class="interp"><strong>Interpretation:</strong> Die Auswahl ist ein Datenmodell-Entscheid: kleine, logisch getrennte Zustände profitieren von Schlüsseln; zusammenhängende oder streamartige Inhalte passen eher zur Datei-Schnittstelle. Sie folgt aus den unterschiedlichen, in der Spezifikation beschriebenen Zugriffsmodellen.</p><h4>Betriebsmodell und Datenhaltbarkeit</h4><p>Ein geöffneter Key-Value Storage arbeitet zunächst auf temporären Daten. <code>SyncToStorage</code> schreibt alle Änderungen seit Öffnen oder letzter Synchronisierung dauerhaft und aktualisiert konfigurierte Redundanz; ohne Synchronisierung werden Änderungen beim Schließen oder Neustart verworfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.3">SWS Persistency §7.3 „Key-Value Storage specific Features“</a></p><p>Bei Dateien wird die konkrete Datei über einen Accessor geöffnet. Schreibzugriffe können über <code>SyncToFile</code> gezielt in den physischen Speicher übertragen werden; Ownership des Accessors ist exklusiv. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=section.7.4">SWS Persistency §7.4 „File Storage specific Features“</a></p><h4>Schutz, Wiederherstellung und Ressourcen</h4><p>Redundanz kann Integrität über Prüfsummen oder mehrere Kopien absichern; bei nicht behebbaren Befunden kann ein Recovery-Report-Callback die Anwendung informieren. Eine Wiederherstellung kann initiale oder ältere Daten ergeben und ist daher fachlich zu prüfen. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.4">SWS Persistency §7.2.4 „Redundancy Concepts“</a></p><p>Der konfigurierte Höchstwert begrenzt tatsächlich belegten Speicher. Die Größenabfragen enthalten Metadaten sowie Redundanz- und Backupbedarf und können bei offenem Storage oder parallelen Operationen ungenau sein. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.6">SWS Persistency §7.2.6 „Resource Management Concepts“</a></p><h4>Installation, Update und Rollback</h4><p>Die Target Configuration kann vordefinierte Werte und Dateien einbringen. Während der Verifikationsphase kann <code>UpdatePersistency</code> Änderungen nach neuen Konfigurationsdaten ausführen; nach erfolgreicher Finalisierung entfernt <code>CleanUpPersistency</code> Sicherungsdaten. Ist eine ältere Konfiguration aktiviert, erfolgt abhängig von der gespeicherten Backupversion eine Wiederherstellung oder Neuinstallation. <a class="docref" href="https://www.autosar.org/fileadmin/standards/R25-11/AP/AUTOSAR_AP_SWS_Persistency.pdf#nameddest=subsection.7.2.5">SWS Persistency §7.2.5 „Installation and Update of Persistent Data“</a></p><div Specification of Persistency
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
1 Introduction and Functional Overview
This document is the software specification of the
Persistency functional
cluster
within the
Adaptive Platform
. The
Persistency functional clus-
ter
will be referenced as
Persistency
in the remainder of this document.
Persistency
offers mechanisms to
Adaptive Applications
and other
func-
tional clusters
to store information in the non-volatile memory of a machine. The
data is available over boot and ignition cycles.
The
Persistency
will typically be implemented as a library that runs within a
Pro-
cess
of an
Adaptive Application
, with the rights of that
Process
.

Persistency
distinguishes data integrity, which is ensured by
the configured
redundancy
, from structural integrity, i.e. the
readability of the structure of a
Key-Value Storage
or
File

4 Constraints and Assumptions
4.1 Known Limitations

Although a
Key-Value Storage
and
File Storage
can be configured as
write-only, the current API always allows read access. Read access is even pos-
sible when a
file
has been opened with
ara::per::FileStorage::Open-
FileWriteOnly
.
4.2 Constraints on Configuration
There are several constraints on the
Persistency
configuration that need to be ob-
served by the tooling which creates/processes this part of the
Execution Manifest
.
These constraints are defined in [3].
4.3 Assumptions about the Implementation of Persistency
Persistency
can be implemented with different internal architectures, and at the
same time,
applications
and other
functional clusters
expect a well defined
behavior that is independent of the actual implementation of
Persistency
. There-
fore, the specification in this document needs to be sufficiently generic to cover the
underlying differences. As usual in AUTOSAR Adaptive, the actual implementation is
not defined by the specification and is therefore entirely up to the vendor of
Persis-
tency
.
The following subsections list some of the possible implementations of
Persistency
.
4.3.1 Library Only
In this scenario,
Persistency
consists solely of a library. The manifest is partly used
to configure the compilation of the library (design time parts) and partly transferred to
a configuration file that is read by
Persistency
at run-time (deployment parts).
There is still some freedom regarding the storage of
metadata
and actual data, and
regarding the points in time when
elements
of a
storage
are checked regarding re-
dundancy or authenticity or when they are decrypted. E.g. the whole
File Storage
could be checked when it is opened or the single
files
could be checked when they
are opened.

Specification of Persistency
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
4.3.2 Using a Central Daemon
In this scenario, the
Persistency
library connects in the background to a daemon
via some IPC mechanism. The manifest influences again the compilation of the library
part and is also transferred to configuration files for the library part and possibly also
the daemon.
An implementer has the same freedom regarding data storage, encryption, and checks
for redundancy and authenticity as in the last scenario. But an additional challenge is
that the communication channel between library and daemon can be lost at any time,
resulting in additional potential errors.
4.3.3 Based on a File System
Both a library and a daemon can access
storage
using the file system services of
the operating system. In this case, because AUTOSAR Adaptive is based on POSIX,
the file systems will be mounted with specific options that are out of control of the
Persistency
implementation, but influence the point in time when written data ac-
tually appears on the disc. Due to this, it is not possible to guarantee synchronous
behavior for calls like
ara::per::KeyValueStorage::SyncToStorage
or
ara::
per::ReadWriteAccessor::SyncToFile
.
4.3.4 Direct Access to Storage Hardware
Independently of whether a daemon is used or not,
Persistency
can be implemented
to access hardware devices like flash memory directly. These devices have the intrinsic
problem that the signal that can be read from each memory cell is reduced over time,
mainly influenced by the number of write accesses. In the end, the cell will produce
arbitrary values on each read access.
Unfortunately, the distribution of write accesses in typical systems is very uneven.
Some parameters might be updated a few times a second, while some code may stay
untouched for the whole life time of the ECU. To avoid early read errors, wear leveling
should be deployed, such that frequent updates of single data elements are distributed
over the whole memory area.
On the other hand, most operating systems include a file system or at least a flash
driver that takes care of wear leveling, such that a typical implementation of the
Per-
sistency
will not have to care about the wear leveling. This use case is therefore not
described in any detail in this specification.

Specification of Persistency
AUTOSAR AP R23-11
7 Functional Specification
7.1 The Architecture of Persistency
The
Persistency
offers two different mechanisms to access persistent memory:
Key-Value Storages
offer access to a set of
keys
with associated
values
(similar
to a database), while
File Storages
offer access to a set of
files
(similar to a
directory of a file system).
The typical usage of the
Persistency
within an
Adaptive Application
is de-
picted in Figure 7.1. As shown there, an
Adaptive Application
can use a combi-
nation of multiple
Key-Value Storages
and multiple
File Storages
. Of course,
the same applies to other
functional clusters
using
Persistency
.

tional Clusters
can be modeled similarly to
Adaptive Applications
.

Usage of base classes in the manifest
For simplification reasons, the information that applies to both the
Key-Value Stor-
ages
and the
File Storages
is collected in base classes in the
manifest
, namely
in
PersistencyInterface
for
PersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface
and
PersistencyFileStorageInterface
, and in
PersistencyDeployment
for
PersistencyKeyValueStorage
and
PersistencyFileStorage
.
Likewise, the common information about
key-value pairs
and
files
is collected
in
PersistencyInterfaceElement
for
PersistencyDataElement
and
Per-
sistencyFileElement
, and in
PersistencyDeploymentElement
for
Persis-
tencyKeyValuePair
and
PersistencyFile
.

7.1.2 Key-Value Storages in the Manifest
Every
Key-Value Storage
is either represented by a
PortPrototype
typed by
a
PersistencyKeyValueStorageInterface
in the application design for the re-
spective
AdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType
, or by a
FunctionalClus-
terInteractsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping
, and in both cases by a
PersistencyKeyValueStorage
containing deployment information. Every
Key-
-Value Storage
can hold multiple
key-value pairs
.
Key-value pairs
can
be added and removed at run-time by the
Adaptive Application
or
Functional
Cluster
using the
Persistency
API (see subsubsection 8.2.5.8 and subsubsection
8.2.5.9).
A
Key-Value Storage
with predefined
key-value pairs
can be deployed with
default data during installation or update of an
Adaptive Application
or
Func-
tional Cluster
. This operation is (indirectly) triggered by the
Update and Con-
figuration Management
[7] during installation or update using the deployment in-
formation and data provided by the
software package
of the
Adaptive Appli-
cation
or
Functional Cluster
. See subsection 7.2.6.
The link between application design and deployment information of a
Key-
-Value Storage
is represented by
PersistencyPortPrototypeToKeyVal-
ueStorageMapping
, which refers to a
PortPrototype
typed by a
Persis-
tencyKeyValueStorageInterface
, the corresponding
PersistencyKeyVal-
ueStorage
, and a
Process
.
7.1.3 File Storages in the Manifest
Every
File Storage
is represented by a
PortPrototype
typed by a
Per-
sistencyFileStorageInterface
in the application design for the respective
AdaptiveApplicationSwComponentType
, or by a
FunctionalClusterInter-
actsWithPersistencyDeploymentMapping
, and in both cases by a
Persis-
tencyFileStorage
containing deployment information. Every
File Storage
can
hold multiple
files
as described in [3]. Similar to the
key-value pairs
mentioned
above,
files
can be created and deleted at run-time by the
Adaptive Applica-
tion
or
Functional Cluster
using the
Persistency
API (see subsubsection
8.3.11.11, subsubsection 8.3.11.13, and subsubsection 8.3.11.5).
A
File Storage
with predefined
files
with initial content can be deployed dur-
ing installation or update. This operation is also (indirectly) triggered by the
Up-
date and Configuration Management
[7]. All needed deployment information

AUTOSAR AP R23-11
7.2 General Features of Persistency
[SWS_PER_00002]
d
All specified classes within the
Persistency
shall reside within
the C++ namespace
ara::per
.
c
(RS_AP_00115)
7.2.1 Functional Cluster Lifecycle
7.2.1.1 Initialization and Shutdown of Persistency
Using
ara::core::Initialize
and
ara::core::Deinitialize
, the applica-
tion initializes and de-initializes all
functional clusters
with direct ARA interfaces
(i.e. the
Adaptive Platform Foundation

7.2.3 Parallel Access to Persistent Data
According to [8], the
persistent data
is local to one
Process
. Therefore,
Per-
sistency
will never share
persistent data
between two (or more)
Process
es,
even of the same
Executable
. The background of this decision is that
Persistency
should not provide an additional communication path for
applications
besides the
mechanisms provided by the
functional cluster
Communication Management
(e.g. using ara::com).
[SWS_PER_00309]
d
Persistent data
shall always be local to one
Process
.

(RS_PER_00001)
If
persistent data
needs to be accessed by multiple
Process
es (of the same or
different
applications
), it is the duty of the application designer to provide
Service
Interfaces
for communication.
Persistency
is, on the other hand, prepared to handle concurrent access from mul-
tiple threads of the same
application
, running in the context of the same
Process
.
To create shared access to a
Key-Value Storage
or
File Storage
, either the
ara::per::SharedHandle
returned by
ara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage
and
ara::per::OpenFileStorage
can be passed on (i.e. copied) to another thread, or
ara::per::OpenKeyValueStorage
and
ara::per::OpenFileStorage
can be
called in independent threads for the same
Key-Value Storage
or
File Storage
,
respectively. All operations of the
Key-Value Storage
and
File Storage
support
concurrent access from multiple threads, though operations like
ara::per::Recov-
erKeyValueStorage
and
ara::per::ResetKeyValueStorage
or
ara::per::
RecoverAllFiles
and
ara::per::ResetAllFiles
will only succeed when the
corresponding
Key-Value Storage
or
File Storage
is not opened.
